Behold, the glory of the LORD appeared in the cloud –Exo 16:10.

What a strange phenomenon is this concentrated mass of vapor that navigates the sky above us. In one instance, a cloud can minister such immense blessedness and hope, while in another it can be the instigator of nagging uncertainty and even the arousal of ragged fear. Clouds were often, no doubt, the welcome shade to the heads of weary fishermen upon Galilee and the propagator of hope to the toiling farmer. How often these clouds part at midday to allow the sun’s beaming rays access to the earth. Then in the evening, they provide the opaque structure for the exquisite beauty of a silver lineation.

We may marvel to see an airplane weighing over 700,000 pounds mount up with wings and soar through the heavens, yet a cloud can carry millions of tons of water without any of the dynamics of human intervention. Clouds are formed when moist, warm air rises to a cooler elevation and water condenses onto microscopic “seeds” such as dust, ash, or bacteria. If there’s more water vapor than places on which it can condense, then ice crystals can also serve as seeds and take on moisture—He bindeth up the waters in his thick clouds; and the cloud is not rent under them –Job 26:8. Eventually, these seeds become too heavy for updrafts to support, and then, behold, it is time for the umbrella.

To the parched land in Elijah’s day, the smallest of clouds (like a man’s hand in 1 Kings 18:44) was the answer from the Almighty that He was again prepared to bless His people with rain. Yet, to others like Job and Jeremiah, the cloud represented the ultimate emblem of doubt, despair, and discouragement. Terrors are turned upon me: they pursue my soul as the wind: and my welfare passeth away as a cloud –Job 30:15, and Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that our prayer should not pass through –Lam 3:44. It is often in such stressful conditions that God chooses to hide Himself in a cloud. At these times, we grope through the thick foreboding fog in search of the pathway of light, but we find it not. In our discouragement, we may long for the beam of a cloudless day, but it eludes us. We know that God is in the midst of the mist, but we cannot apprehend Him, nor see His blessedness. With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it not to shine by the cloud that cometh betwixt –Job 36:32.

Why would our God, who loves to commune with us, the vessels of His own creation, choose to hide Himself in a cloud? Why does He often hide His will from our searching and aching hearts? Our finite minds often wonder what glory could possibly arise from such a seemingly distant God, and …to what purpose is this waste –Mat 26:8. While we would never expect it to be God’s divine plan to leave us in a foggy stupor forever, it may be His will for a time. Like a stroll through the valley of the shadow of death, there can be eternal character wrought in the soul who has experienced a seasonal lack of clarity in their path. We are well aware that the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day –Pro 4:18. Still, most of us have, at times, experienced the hopeless fog that surrounds our present and our future. In these times, we meet with darkness in the daytime, and grope in the noonday as in the night –Job 5:14. In our bedraggled discouragement, we can easily lose sight of the goodness of God. Our resulting lack of thankfulness is a sure road to a host of other temptations, while the giant of despair rises overhead in an attempt to weaken our resistance to sin.

We know that Elijah was a man subject to like passions as we are –Jam 5:17. Yet, few of us have ever experienced a victory as exhilarating as he did when he triumphed over the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel. Still, many of us can well relate to the discouragement that followed as he came unto Horeb and lodged in a cave there. This is the same place as Mount Sinai where the first great mountain scene opened before us in the Scriptures. Then it was Moses who met God in the cloud. The law was given, and God’s glory was so marvelously manifested and so terrible was the sight, that Moses said, I exceedingly fear and quake –Heb 12:21. This mount that might be touched was a formidable and intimidating mountain flanked by splintering dark granite peaks and stern ridges of indescribable grandeur. The bold and awful front of Horeb, rises in frowning majesty from twelve hundred to fifteen hundred feet in perpendicular height.

With Elijah’s vision clouded over and his spirit ebbing away at an all-time low, God responded to him in astounding methodology—…And, behold, the LORD passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the LORD; but the LORD was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the LORD was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the LORD was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice. And it was so, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went out… –1 Kin 19:11-13.

Somehow, we have come to believe that an earthshaking experience is the epitome of God’s manifest presence. We reckon that God was closer to Elijah on Mt. Carmel than He was on Mt. Horeb. It was Elijah’s “day in the sun” while speaking on Mt. Carmel. He chided the people and mocked the prophets. He preached boldly in the name of the Lord and commanded the people to repent of their duplicity. But now his voice has been silenced and he is listening … listening to the still small voice calling into account his own actions and ambitions. Thus, if we will but stop and listen, the memory of our dismal failures will escort us to the front porch of our Lord, rather than allow us to glory in our perceived successes.

This is the blessed ministration of the cloud. It is often the vehicle that the Lord will use to bring us to the place where we can truly receive His manifest glory in our hearts. This is not the white, fluffy, cumulus clouds of a balmy summer day but, rather, the flat and featureless stratus clouds that blanket the heavens from east to west and totally eclipse all the rays of heavenly sunshine. They can enshroud the day at high noon with an arsenal of gloom that rankles our hearts to the core. The little things, that on other days had little effect on our attitudes, now seem to tower as giants before us. We may face advents that we know are beyond our control, but our minds refuse to enter into rest. In times like these, if there happens to be an unfortunate soul on the other end of our conversation experiencing a similar plight, we may experience firsthand that …man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward –Job 5:7. At other times, our melancholy mood may be content to withdraw and feed itself with our own reclusive pity and foggy misery.

Some, in their desperation, turn to medication for the mind and there find a limited valve of relief. But God has not brought us into the cloud so that we may seek the help of physicians and psychologists. The ministration of the cloud is to shut off all other alternatives so that we may receive of Him the full blessedness of His consolation. God is willing that we should sacrifice the shimmering sunshine of today for the fullness of His presence tomorrow.

Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away –Jas 4:14. In bygone years, I have preached on this verse, exhorting souls concerning the brevity of life and encouraging them to not squander their years away. But I had totally ignored the foundation of it—ye know not what shall be on the morrow. This, perhaps, seems trite to the young at heart, but as the fruit of my age continues to ripen, I have a growing appreciation for the common and obvious idioms. Our modern scientific world is so adamantly pursuing the love of life that it cannot appreciate the life of love that is begotten through suffering. While those who, in ages past, suffered in the flesh and ceased from sin (1 Pet 4:1), I see no reason why those who experience the frail sufferings of a clouded mind may not share the same glory if they will but endure and trust to God the results.

We are an arrogant people who lean on the predictions of tomorrow. We fancy that we can plan our retirement and schedule our life events with immaculate detail. The weather forecasters tell us of tomorrows temperature so that we can meticulously plan our day. Our insurance gives assurance that we will not be subject to future poverty. Our freezers and bank accounts are full enough to see us well past tomorrow, and we have grown accustomed to believing that we …sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow –Rev 18:7. Yet the sorrow of heart cannot be so easily absolved by earthly amenities. Our life is a vapour (cloud) because we …know not what shall be on the morrow… –Jas 4:14. In spite of all our technology we still cannot absolve that fact. It is here that we must lay aside all our intuitions, expectations, and ambitions of what our life ought to be and find our God in the cloud.

He holdeth back the face of his throne, and spreadeth his cloud upon it –Job 26:9. To what benefit is the cloud covering the face of God’s throne? If it were easily beholden, most of us would be content to dwell with Him from afar. However, due to the impending fog, we must draw nigh to experience His fullness. How thankful we ought to be that it is thus, for how devastating would be our spiritual loss if it were not so.

If our self-sufficient life was always vibrantly full and God were easily apprehended, we would lose…

…Faith

We seek a guarantee that our trials will end happily ever after and that our prayers will naturally become unnecessary. In faith, we believe in God’s provision, but the fact that we know not what a day will bring demands that we fall upon our feeble knees and pray. There may be many things that make it hard for us to trust in God, but the shrouded tomorrow makes it easier. Researchers have spent millions in their efforts to control the weather. They have sown every imaginable cloud seed into the air in efforts to produce rain clouds. After reviewing 40 years of cloud-seeding efforts in an area north of Israel, researchers at Tel Aviv University have concluded that cloud seeding doesn’t actually produce any additional precipitation. How thankful we should be. The more we can control the unknown morrow, the less faith in the Master of the Universe we need.

Jacob, in leaving behind an angry brother, a disappointed father, and a severed tie with his mother, faced an altogether unknown future. This is a part of the ladder to the throne and it fortifies our commitment to our omnipotent God. Now we know in part and we see in part. Perhaps that fractional sliver brings us more inner wealth than if the whole were fully understood. If our future were amply within our manipulative power, we would formulate a perfect utopia supplied with the perfect number of children living sumptuously in the perfect home supported by the perfect job surrounded by perfect behavior that is perfectly sterile and dead.

…Hope

I question if we realize how deeply our debt is to the unexpected. The Hebrew writer declares our hope to be …an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast… –Heb 6:19. Children are happy because they have big dreams. Often the anticipation and planning of an event is almost as thrilling as the excursion itself. Every day is a bright new window to the unspoiled, hopeful mind. Experiences can often bring us to the brink of cynicism and bitterness when viewed through yesterday’s disappointments. Jacob, upon the marvelous reunification with his son, Joseph, still remarked, few and evil have been my days. Though it is naturally so, it needs not to be. Paul states …that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope –Rom 5:3-4. Surely, if we knew what was in store tomorrow (both good and evil) the invigorating element of hope would dwindle. Eve feigned that life would be better if she could only secure more knowledge. But what blessed hope was forfeited in her lustful pursuit of clarity.

…Love

There is a wistful tenderness in love that nothing but uncertainty can give. It is uncertain wonder that encompasses the way of a young man with a maid. The unknown perils of tomorrow drive a mother to love and prayer for her children. It is the vision of a brighter tomorrow for his family that moves a father to diligence in his daily work. Wherever a husband and his wife are knit together in Biblical oneness of holy matrimony, the mystery that envelops tomorrow is like the minor chord in a great melody. It speaks in joy of a suggested sorrow and brightens sorrow with encircling joy. Would Jacob’s seven-year wait have seemed like a few days if he had known what the morrow would bring? If we knew everything, love would be too hard. If we knew everything, love would be too easy. If we knew everything, we would be brokenhearted. If we knew everything, we would be unconcerned. In other words, it makes us stronger to not know the worst and it makes us more tender to not know the best. For in our clouded and darkened lens there …abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity –1 Cor 13:13.

It is no coincidence that while the disciples …beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight –Act 1:9. And so we dare not be surprised that, at times, we shall be called to suffer the mental strain and stress of an obscure and unknown tomorrow. …For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away –Jas 4:14. There is coming a day when we shall …see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory –Luk 21:27. And again it is written, Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him … Even so, Amen –Rev 1:7.

Tazama, utukufu wa BWANA ukaonekana katika wingu –Kut 16:10.

Ni jambo la ajabu jinsi gani mkusanyiko huu mnene wa mvuke unavyosafiri katika anga lililo juu yetu. Katika tukio moja, wingu linaweza kuleta baraka na tumaini kubwa sana, ilhali katika jingine linaweza kuwa chanzo cha mashaka yanayosumbua na hata kuchochea hofu kali. Bila shaka, mara nyingi mawingu yalikuwa kivuli kilichokaribishwa na vichwa vya wavuvi waliochoka kwenye Galilaya na chanzo cha tumaini kwa mkulima mwenye taabu. Mara nyingi jinsi gani mawingu haya hutengana adhuhuri na kuruhusu miale inayong’aa ya jua kuifikia dunia. Kisha jioni, yanatoa mandhari tulivu ambamo uzuri wa ajabu wa mstari wa fedha hung’aa.

Tunaweza kushangaa kuona ndege yenye uzito wa zaidi ya pauni 700,000 ikipaa kwa mabawa na kuruka juu angani, ilhali wingu linaweza kubeba mamilioni ya tani za maji bila nguvu zozote za binadamu kuingilia kati. Mawingu hutokea wakati hewa yenye unyevunyevu na joto inapoinuka hadi kwenye kimo chenye baridi zaidi, na maji huganda juu ya “mbegu” ndogo sana kama vile vumbi, majivu au bakteria. Ikiwa kuna mvuke wa maji mwingi kuliko sehemu zinazoweza kugandia, basi fuwele za barafu pia zinaweza kutumika kama mbegu na kuvuta unyevunyevu—Huyafunga maji katika mawingu yake mazito; wala wingu halipasuki kwa uzito wake –Ayu 26:8. Hatimaye, mbegu hizi huwa nzito sana hivi kwamba mikondo ya hewa inayopaa haiwezi kuzishikilia, kisha, tazama, wakati wa mwavuli huwa umefika.

Kwa nchi iliyokauka sana katika siku za Eliya, wingu dogo kabisa (kama mkono wa mtu katika 1 Wafalme 18:44) lilikuwa jibu kutoka kwa Mwenyezi kwamba alikuwa tayari tena kuwabariki watu wake kwa mvua. Hata hivyo, kwa wengine kama Ayubu na Yeremia, wingu liliwakilisha ishara kuu ya mashaka, kukata tamaa na kuvunjika moyo. Vitisho vimenigeukia; vinaifuatilia nafsi yangu kama upepo; na heri yangu hupita kama wingu –Ayu 30:15, na Umejifunika kwa wingu, ili maombi yetu yasipite –Omb 3:44. Mara nyingi ni katika hali hizo zenye msongo ambapo Mungu huchagua kujificha katika wingu. Nyakati hizo, tunapapasa-papasa katika ukungu mzito na wa kuogofya tukitafuta njia ya nuru, lakini hatuipati. Tunapovunjika moyo, huenda tukatamani miale ya siku isiyo na mawingu, lakini hutukwepa. Tunajua kwamba Mungu yumo katikati ya ukungu, lakini hatuwezi kumtambua wala kuuona wema wake. Hufunika nuru kwa mawingu; wala haiamuru iangaze kwa sababu ya wingu lililo katikati –Ayu 36:32.

Kwa nini Mungu wetu, anayependa kushirikiana nasi, viumbe alivyoviumba mwenyewe, achague kujificha katika wingu? Kwa nini mara nyingi huficha mapenzi yake yasifikiwe na mioyo yetu inayotafuta na kuumia? Akili zetu zenye mipaka mara nyingi hujiuliza ni utukufu gani ambao ungeweza kutokana na Mungu aliye mbali kiasi hicho, na …upotevu huu ni wa nini? –Mt 26:8. Ingawa hatutarajii kamwe kwamba mpango wa Mungu ni kutuacha katika hali ya kuchanganyikiwa na ukungu milele, huenda hilo likawa mapenzi yake kwa muda fulani. Kama matembezi katika bonde la uvuli wa mauti, nafsi iliyopitia kipindi cha kutokuwa na uwazi kuhusu njia yake inaweza kukuza tabia ya milele. Tunafahamu vyema kwamba njia ya wenye haki ni kama nuru ing’aayo, ikizidi kung’aa hata mchana mkamilifu –Mit 4:18. Hata hivyo, wengi wetu tumepitia nyakati fulani ukungu usio na tumaini unaozingira wakati wetu wa sasa na wa baadaye. Nyakati hizo, hukutana na giza wakati wa mchana, na kupapasa-papasa adhuhuri kama wakati wa usiku –Ayu 5:14. Katika kuvunjika moyo kwetu, ni rahisi kupoteza mtazamo wa wema wa Mungu. Ukosefu wetu wa shukrani unaotokana na hali hiyo ni njia ya hakika ya kutupeleka kwenye majaribu mengine mengi, huku jitu la kukata tamaa likiinuka juu yetu likijaribu kudhoofisha upinzani wetu dhidi ya dhambi.

Tunajua kwamba Eliya alikuwa mwanadamu mwenye tabia moja na sisi –Yak 5:17. Hata hivyo, ni wachache wetu ambao wamewahi kupata ushindi wa kusisimua kama ule alioupata alipowashinda manabii wa Baali kwenye Mlima Karmeli. Lakini wengi wetu tunaweza kuelewa vyema kuvunjika moyo kulikofuata alipofika Horebu na kukaa katika pango. Hapa ni mahali pale pale pa Mlima Sinai ambapo tukio kuu la kwanza la mlimani lilianza mbele yetu katika Maandiko. Wakati huo Musa ndiye aliyekutana na Mungu katika wingu. Sheria ilitolewa, na utukufu wa Mungu ulidhihirishwa kwa namna ya ajabu sana, hata huo ulikuwa ni wa kutisha sana, hata Musa akasema, Naogopa mno na kutetemeka –Ebr 12:21. Huu mlima ulioweza kuguswa ulikuwa mlima wa kutisha na wa kuogofya, uliopakana na vilele vya granite nyeusi vilivyopasuka na miinuko mikali yenye fahari isiyoelezeka. Uso wa Horebu wenye ujasiri na wa kutisha huinuka kwa fahari ya kuogofya, kutoka urefu wa futi mia moja na ishirini hadi mia moja na hamsini kwa wima.

Maono ya Eliya yalipofunikwa na wingu na roho yake ikazidi kudhoofika mpaka kufikia hali ya chini kabisa, Mungu alimjibu kwa njia ya kushangaza—…Na tazama, BWANA akapita; upepo mkubwa wenye nguvu ukapasua milima na kuvunja-vunja miamba mbele za BWANA; lakini BWANA hakuwamo katika upepo ule; na baada ya upepo tetemeko la nchi; lakini BWANA hakuwamo katika lile tetemeko la nchi; na baada ya tetemeko la nchi kukawa na moto; lakini BWANA hakuwamo katika moto ule; na baada ya moto sauti ndogo, tulivu. Ikawa, Eliya alipoisikia, akajifunika uso wake kwa vazi lake, akatoka nje… –1 Fal 19:11-13.

Kwa namna fulani, tumefikia kuamini kwamba tukio linalotikisa dunia ndilo kilele cha uwepo wa Mungu unaodhihirika. Tunadhani Mungu alikuwa karibu zaidi na Eliya kwenye Mlima Karmeli kuliko alivyokuwa kwenye Mlima Horebu. Ilikuwa “siku yake ya kung’aa” Eliya alipohubiri kwenye Mlima Karmeli. Aliwakemea watu na kuwadhihaki manabii. Alihubiri kwa ujasiri kwa jina la Bwana na kuwaamuru watu watubu kwa sababu ya unafiki wao. Lakini sasa sauti yake imenyamazishwa, naye anasikiliza … akisikiliza sauti ndogo, tulivu inayomwita awajibike kwa matendo na matamanio yake mwenyewe. Hivyo basi, tukisimama tu na kusikiliza, kumbukumbu ya kushindwa kwetu kwa kusikitisha itatuongoza mpaka kwenye baraza la mbele la Bwana wetu, badala ya kuturuhusu kujisifu kwa mafanikio tunayodhani tumepata.

Huu ndio huduma yenye baraka ya wingu. Mara nyingi ndilo chombo ambacho Bwana hutumia kutuleta mahali ambapo tunaweza kupokea kwa kweli utukufu wake unaodhihirika mioyoni mwetu. Haya si mawingu meupe, laini ya cumulus ya siku tulivu ya kiangazi, bali ni mawingu ya stratus yaliyo tambarare na yasiyo na umbo maalumu, yanayofunika anga kuanzia mashariki hadi magharibi na kuzuia kabisa miale yote ya jua la mbinguni. Yanaweza kuufunika mchana wakati wa adhuhuri kwa giza tele linalochoma mioyo yetu hadi kilindini. Mambo madogo ambayo siku nyingine hayakuwa na athari kubwa kwa mitazamo yetu sasa yanaonekana kama majitu yanayotuogopesha. Huenda tukakabiliwa na mambo yanayotokea ambayo tunajua hatuwezi kuyadhibiti, lakini akili zetu zinakataa kutulia. Nyakati kama hizo, ikiwa kwa bahati mbaya kuna mtu upande wa pili wa mazungumzo yetu anayepitia shida kama hiyo, tunaweza kujionea wenyewe kwamba …mwanadamu amezaliwa ili apate taabu, kama vile cheche za moto zirukavyo juu –Ayu 5:7. Nyakati nyingine, hali yetu ya huzuni inaweza kuridhika kujitenga na kujilisha kwa kujihurumia na taabu zetu wenyewe za upweke na ukungu.

Wengine, kwa kukata tamaa, hugeukia dawa za akili na huko hupata nafuu kwa kiwango fulani. Lakini Mungu hakutuingiza katika wingu ili tutafute msaada wa waganga na wanasaikolojia. Huduma ya wingu ni kufunga njia zote nyingine ili tupokee kutoka kwake faraja yake iliyojaa baraka. Mungu yuko tayari tutekeleze jua linalong’aa la leo kwa ajili ya utimilifu wa uwepo wake kesho.

Maana hamjui yatakayokuwako kesho. Maana maisha yenu ni nini? Maana ninyi ni mvuke, uonekanao kwa kitambo, kisha hutoweka –Yak 4:14. Miaka iliyopita, nilihubiri juu ya mstari huu, nikizihimiza nafsi kuhusu ufupi wa maisha na kuzitia moyo zisipoteze miaka yao. Lakini nilikuwa nimepuuza kabisa msingi wake—hamjui yatakayokuwako kesho. Huenda hili likaonekana jambo dogo kwa wale walio na moyo mchanga, lakini kadiri matunda ya umri wangu yanavyoendelea kuiva, ndivyo ninavyozidi kuthamini misemo ya kawaida na iliyo wazi. Ulimwengu wetu wa kisasa wa kisayansi unafuata kwa msisitizo mkubwa sana kupenda maisha kiasi kwamba hauwezi kuthamini maisha ya upendo yanayozaliwa kupitia mateso. Ingawa wale walioteseka katika mwili na kuacha dhambi zamani (1 Pet 4:1), sioni sababu kwa nini wale wanaopitia mateso dhaifu ya akili iliyofunikwa na wingu wasishiriki utukufu huo huo, ikiwa tu watavumilia na kumwachia Mungu matokeo.

Sisi ni watu wenye kiburi tunaotegemea utabiri wa kesho. Tunajidanganya kwamba tunaweza kupanga kustaafu kwetu na kupanga matukio ya maisha yetu kwa undani usio na dosari. Watabiri wa hali ya hewa hutuambia halijoto ya kesho ili tuweze kupanga siku yetu kwa umakini. Bima yetu hutuhakikishia kwamba hatutakabiliwa na umaskini siku zijazo. Friza zetu na akaunti zetu za benki zimejaa vya kutosha kutuendesha hata baada ya kesho, nasi tumezoea kuamini kwamba …naketi kama malkia, wala mimi si mjane, wala sitaona huzuni –Ufu 18:7. Hata hivyo, huzuni ya moyo haiwezi kuondolewa kwa urahisi hivyo kwa huduma za duniani. Maisha yetu ni mvuke (wingu) kwa sababu …hatujui yatakayokuwako kesho… –Yak 4:14. Licha ya teknolojia yetu yote, bado hatuwezi kuondoa ukweli huo. Hapo ndipo tunapopaswa kuweka kando hisia zetu, matarajio yetu na matamanio yetu yote kuhusu maisha yetu yanavyopaswa kuwa, na kumkuta Mungu wetu katika wingu.

Huzuia uso wa kiti chake cha enzi, na kutandaza wingu lake juu yake –Ayu 26:9. Kuna faida gani wingu linapofunika uso wa kiti cha enzi cha Mungu? Kama kingeonekana kwa urahisi, wengi wetu tungeridhika kukaa naye kwa mbali. Hata hivyo, kwa sababu ya ukungu unaotukaribia, ni lazima tusogee karibu ili kuonja utimilifu wake. Tunapaswa kushukuru sana kwamba mambo yako hivi, kwa maana hasara yetu ya kiroho ingekuwa kubwa jinsi gani kama isingekuwa hivyo.

Kama maisha yetu ya kujitegemea yangeendelea kuwa na uhai mwingi daima na Mungu angeweza kutambuliwa kwa urahisi, tungepoteza…

…Imani

Tunataka uhakikisho kwamba majaribu yetu yataishia kwa furaha ya kudumu na kwamba maombi yetu kwa kawaida hayatakuwa tena na ulazima. Kwa imani, tunaamini katika riziki ya Mungu, lakini ukweli kwamba hatujui siku italeta nini unatuhitaji tupige magoti yetu dhaifu na kuomba. Huenda kuna mambo mengi yanayotufanya iwe vigumu kumtumaini Mungu, lakini kutokujulikana kwa kesho iliyofunikwa na wingu hurahisisha jambo hilo. Watafiti wametumia mamilioni katika juhudi zao za kudhibiti hali ya hewa. Wametawanya kila aina ya mbegu za mawingu zinazoweza kuwazika angani kwa juhudi za kutokeza mawingu ya mvua. Baada ya kukagua miaka 40 ya juhudi za kutawanya mbegu za mawingu katika eneo lililo kaskazini mwa Israeli, watafiti katika Chuo Kikuu cha Tel Aviv wamehitimisha kwamba kutawanya mbegu za mawingu kwa kweli hakuleti ongezeko lolote la mvua. Tunapaswa kushukuru sana. Kadiri tunavyoweza kudhibiti kesho isiyojulikana, ndivyo tunavyohitaji imani kidogo kwa Bwana wa Ulimwengu.

Yakobo, alipomwacha nyuma ndugu mwenye hasira, baba aliyekatishwa tamaa, na uhusiano uliokatika na mama yake, alikabili wakati ujao usiojulikana kabisa. Hii ni sehemu ya ngazi inayoelekea kwenye kiti cha enzi, nayo huimarisha kujitoa kwetu kwa Mungu wetu mwenye uweza wote. Sasa tunajua kwa sehemu, na tunaona kwa sehemu. Huenda kipande hicho kidogo kikatuongezea utajiri wa ndani zaidi kuliko kama tungeelewa kila kitu kikamilifu. Kama wakati wetu ujao ungekuwa chini ya uwezo wetu wa kuutengeneza kwa wingi, tungeunda utopia kamilifu yenye idadi kamili ya watoto wanaoishi kwa anasa katika nyumba kamilifu, wakitegemezwa na kazi kamilifu na kuzungukwa na mwenendo mkamilifu ulio tasa na mfu kabisa.

…Tumaini

Najiuliza kama tunatambua jinsi tunavyodaiwa sana na mambo yasiyotazamiwa. Mwandishi wa Waebrania anasema tumaini letu ni …nanga ya nafsi, yenye salama na thabiti… –Ebr 6:19. Watoto huwa na furaha kwa sababu wana ndoto kubwa. Mara nyingi matarajio na mipango ya tukio husisimua karibu sawa na safari yenyewe. Kila siku ni dirisha jipya lenye nuru kwa akili isiyoharibiwa na iliyojaa tumaini. Tunapotazama mambo kupitia masikitiko ya jana, mambo tuliyoyapitia mara nyingi yanaweza kutupeleka ukingoni mwa kuwa na mashaka na uchungu. Yakobo, hata baada ya kuunganishwa tena kwa ajabu na mwanawe Yosefu, bado alisema, siku za maisha yangu zimekuwa chache na mbaya. Ingawa mambo huwa hivyo kwa kawaida, si lazima yawe hivyo. Paulo anasema …dhiki huleta saburi; na saburi huleta utahiniwa; na utahiniwa huleta tumaini –Rum 5:3-4. Hakika, kama tungejua yaliyotusubiri kesho (mazuri na mabaya), kipengele chenye kuchangamsha cha tumaini kingepungua. Hawa alijifanya kwamba maisha yangekuwa bora kama tu angeweza kupata maarifa zaidi. Lakini tumaini lenye baraka jinsi gani alilopoteza katika harakati yake ya kutamani uwazi.

…Upendo

Kuna upole wa mapenzi uliojaa hisia ambao hakuna kitu isipokuwa kutokuwa na uhakika kinachoweza kuleta. Ni mshangao usio na uhakika unaozunguka njia ya kijana na msichana. Hatari zisizojulikana za kesho humsukuma mama kuwapenda watoto wake na kuwaombea. Ni maono ya kesho angavu zaidi kwa familia yake yanayomsukuma baba kufanya kazi yake ya kila siku kwa bidii. Mahali popote ambapo mume na mke wameunganishwa katika umoja wa kibiblia wa ndoa takatifu, fumbo linaloifunika kesho huwa kama noti ndogo katika melodi kuu. Husema kwa furaha kuhusu huzuni inayodokezwa, na kuangaza huzuni kwa furaha inayoizunguka. Je, miaka saba ambayo Yakobo alingoja ingeonekana kama siku chache kama angejua kesho ingeleta nini? Kama tungejua kila kitu, upendo ungekuwa mgumu mno. Kama tungejua kila kitu, upendo ungekuwa rahisi mno. Kama tungejua kila kitu, mioyo yetu ingevunjika. Kama tungejua kila kitu, tusingejali. Kwa maneno mengine, kutokujua mabaya zaidi hutufanya kuwa imara zaidi, na kutokujua mazuri zaidi hutufanya kuwa wapole zaidi. Kwa maana katika mtazamo wetu uliofunikwa na wingu na kutiwa giza, …hudumu imani, tumaini, upendo, haya matatu; na katika hayo lililo kuu ni upendo –1 Kor 13:13.

Si kwa bahati kwamba wanafunzi walipokuwa …wakitazama, akachukuliwa juu; wingu likampokea kutoka machoni pao –Mdo 1:9. Kwa hiyo hatupaswi kushangaa kwamba nyakati fulani tutaitwa kuvumilia mkazo na msongo wa kiakili wa kesho isiyoeleweka na isiyojulikana. …Maana maisha yenu ni nini? Maana ninyi ni mvuke, uonekanao kwa kitambo, kisha hutoweka –Yak 4:14. Siku inakuja ambapo …watamwona Mwana wa Adamu akija katika wingu pamoja na nguvu na utukufu mwingi –Lk 21:27. Tena imeandikwa, Tazama, yuaja pamoja na mawingu; na kila jicho litamwona … Naam, Amina –Ufu 1:7.

If we step back and look at our own life, can we honestly say that we trust in the Lord with all our heart? I often think of my children—they trust in me with all their hearts; there is no fear within them; they do not worry. My prayer is that I can trust in my Heavenly Father in the same way.

Here in Haiti a lot of people are driven by fear. They fear the uncertainty of tomorrow. They fear whether they will find food, work, and clothing. It is the opposite of trusting in God. In the western culture, people don’t fear those things. Food and clothing are easy to find, jobs are plentiful, and medical assistance is just one 911 call away.

The poor people here in Haiti say that it would be easier to trust God if they were in America, but is that truly the case? While very few in America fear whether they will have enough to eat, many fear whether they will be accepted by other people. There are some who may fear having enough money to live, but there are many who fear death. Whatever our fear is, trusting in God is our answer.

Let’s look at the life of David. David was a young boy. When his older brothers went to battle, young David went out to feed his father’s sheep. On the battlefield, there was a giant with the Philistine army named Goliath. He challenged the Israelites by saying that if one man would come out and fight him, the victor’s army would rule the other side. In 1 Samuel 17:10-11 we read that Goliath said, …I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together. When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.

Later on, we read that Jesse, David’s father, sent him to the place of battle to take some food to his older brothers. David arrived at the place of battle, and he heard Goliath speaking these same words. When David saw that the men of Israel were all afraid, he did not understand. Why were God’s people afraid of this uncircumcised Philistine?

Even though David was young, he was no amateur when it came to putting his trust in God. While he was watching his father’s sheep, most likely he talked much with God, asking Him to help guard the sheep. One day a bear came out to attack the sheep, and David killed the bear. Another day a lion came out to eat some sheep. Again, the God-trusting, fearless youth faced the threat and killed the lion. Now, facing a seemingly greater threat, David simply asks, …who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God? –1Sa 17:26. David went to King Saul and said, I …will go and fight with this Philistine –1Sa 17:32. Once more putting his trust in his God, David took five smooth stones, ran out to meet the giant, and killed him. Upon seeing this sudden turn of events, the people marveled.

According to Psalm 20:7, when we put our trust in horses and chariots, then it is not in the Lord our God. In Matthew 21:21, the Bible says that with faith we can move mountains. Here in Haiti I have found myself in tough situations where God is my only option. When I have been forced to put my trust in God, I have discovered that He still works miracles. Just like David with the lion, the bear, and the giant, we too can learn that trusting God with our whole heart is the best way and not just a last resort. When we trust in the Lord first, we show the world something amazing—that this God we serve is alive, and that He is real.

Here in Haiti there was a man living in a shack up in the mountains with his wife and three young children. But there was a problem—he was deathly ill. One day he heard about a missionary who often traveled through the mountains. I received a message from him stating that he was almost dead and that he needed me to come and pray for him. I quickly went up to his home. I was amazed at his condition. His weight was probably not much more than 70 pounds. His wife told me that he had been in bed for over a year. He couldn’t talk, he only whispered with deep agonizing breaths. We spent quite a while discussing his life, his sin, and his future. He told me that if God would heal him, he would serve him and trust him for the rest of his life. I believed his sincerity, yet I was scared. I began to pray, but it was certainly not a powerful prayer full of faith. Rather it was a weak, humble cry.

As I went home and throughout that night, he was all I could think about. The devil began his attack. I had many confusing, troubling thoughts, “Did you do everything you could have done? What if he dies? Why didn’t you take him to the hospital?” I went to God in prayer. “Oh God,” I prayed, “this man wanted prayer. He didn’t ask for a hospital; he didn’t ask for medication. Please God, heal this man. If he dies, what will I do the next time? O Father, if not for him, please, heal him for me. I need you to, Father.”

I prayed like I had never prayed before, and then, God gave me peace. The next morning, I hurried up the mountain to his home, but he wasn’t there. “No, Lord!” I thought. I rushed around and poked my head in another shack. What I saw overwhelmed me. He was sitting there with a big smile on his face. His wife said that he had been working in the garden that morning. Repeatedly she said, “God healed him! God healed him!” I’ll never forget the feeling I had as I travelled back down that mountain. My heart welled up with joy and thankfulness. “My God is alive! He can do anything and everything! He is my God!” I thanked and praised Him like I never had before. “The lion” that I had faced was dead, and my faith was growing. The devil doesn’t want us to trust God, because when we put our trust in God, He does big things, and our faith grows.

When we put our trust in God there is a risk—what if God doesn’t work? We could be embarrassed, or worse—“What if I step out in faith and God does nothing?” Remember, it is not faith if we know the outcome. Faith is walking in obedience and believing God’s Word when we do not know the outcome. If God wouldn’t have helped David, Goliath surely would have killed him. It was Daniel’s faith that kept him praying to God, even though he knew a lion’s den awaited him. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego had so much faith in God that they told the king that even if God chose to not deliver them from the fire, that they still would …not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up –Dan 3:18. Then there was Gideon and his three hundred men. The list goes on and on of godly men who put their life on the line, proving that their God was alive.

When we step out in faith, trusting our God, something always happens (sometimes now, sometimes later; sometimes in a way that makes sense, sometimes in a way that seems to make no earthly sense). Yet God does work, and our faith grows. When we truly believe in God, we will trust him. Then, sharing the Gospel message with others is much easier. Just like Joshua did not have a fleet of bulldozers on standby at Jericho, so also we do not need a backup plan when we trust in God.

It is true that the great minds and financial backing of many in America and other modern countries have replaced God. There is a way to do most physical things without God. In fact, most people say that trusting in God is not common sense. If you pray over a sick child, it’s not common sense. If you turn down a high paying job because you don’t believe that it’s God’s will, that’s not common sense. If you sell your possessions and give to the poor, it’s not common sense. These people are right—trusting in God is not common sense. Marching around a wall seven times, believing it will fall down, is not common sense. Going into battle with only 300 men against a great army who were like grasshoppers for multitude is not common sense either. Most things done by God-trusting Christians don’t make sense, but they do show the world that they really do put their trust in God, and that is what will turn the world upside down again, today.

I remember one day very well. I was away from home when I received a phone call from my wife. She told me to come home quickly—it was an emergency! Our two-year-old son had been stung by bees. I rushed home to see the neighborhood in chaos. People where running around everywhere. I found my wife and son at the neighbor’s house, a local pastor. My son lay in the arms of my wife who told me he had been stung several hundred times. The pastor looked at me quite gravely, telling me that if I didn’t get this boy to a hospital right away, he would surely die. I remember thinking one thing—God can heal! I picked up my son and took him across the street to our house, and I prayed. It didn’t take long before he began to recover—by the next day he was back out playing.

Many people here in Haiti take their sick to the witch doctor, and he heals them. It’s just what happens. How much more can our God do! Please don’t misunderstand me. I’m not saying we shouldn’t go to the medical doctor or to the hospital; rather, I’m trying to emphasize that our trust should be in God.

Years ago, I decided to take up a part-time job selling knives. I was to take these knives and travel from home to home. I didn’t have an interest in knives but was just trying to make some extra money. I was a terrible knife salesman. Everywhere I went everyone said no.

One day the boss took me into his office where he told me that he had noticed I wasn’t selling any knives and realized he had forgotten to show me how the knives worked. So, we sat there in his office as he talked about each knife. He had a small pile of kitchen utensils of another brand, which were known for their quality, that he used for a comparison. First, he held up a small piece of leather and asked me to cut it in half with one of the “other” knives. I sawed through the piece of leather with some ease. Then he instructed me to use one of his knives and do the same thing. The new knife sliced through the leather as if it wasn’t even there! I was truly amazed. He then picked up a penny and told me to cut it in half using the “other” scissors. I tried but failed; they simply would not cut it. He then told me to do the same using his scissors. It easily cut through the penny, and again I was amazed at the product. He told me that I now knew that these knives were the best and from now on I should be able to sell them. He was right. I began selling knives everywhere I went! I even remember walking into a poorly kept trailer home without much hope that they would buy. Surprisingly, they bought over $3,000 worth of knives.

The reason I began to make sales is obvious—I believed in my product. Likewise, if we put our trust in God, we will have confidence. In a day when most proclaiming Christians are ashamed of God and ashamed to stand up for truth, we can be a bright and shining light. We can be a people who go out into the world and into our communities with a Gospel that we truly believe in! As we do, the world will see it and respond. Many are seeking; they are looking for answers. When someone asks us a question about why we do the things we do or wear what we wear, what is our reply? Do we reply with confidence? Do we have a ready Bible verse? Or do we get embarrassed and desire a hole to climb into? If the world could see that we are confident in our God, and that we obey him with enthusiasm, it would be a powerful testimony.

I remember traveling through the airport with a small group. As we were standing in line, I overheard a lady ask one of the single sisters in our group why she wore that “thing” on her head. I was excited to listen unnoticed, and I rejoiced as I heard her response. “Have you ever read 1 Corinthians 11? There it instructs us that women should cover their heads. It’s a sign of submission.” The woman was shocked at her answer, saying she never heard that before, and that her father was a pastor. They continued to have a very interesting conversation that ended with that lady desiring to go home and study her Bible.

A tract can do a lot of good; so likewise, a powerful sermon or a printed article, but someone putting all his trust in God is what this world is looking for! They want to “see something that works,” and why not? Our God wants to use us to show Himself strong. Surely each one of us wants to be used by God. We can. Each one of us can. The answer is to trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding –Pro 3:5.

Если взглянуть со стороны на собственную жизнь, можем ли мы честно сказать, что всем сердцем уповаем на Господа? Я часто думаю о своих детях: они всем сердцем доверяют мне, в них нет страха, они не тревожатся. Я молюсь о том, чтобы и сам так же доверял своему Небесному Отцу.

Здесь, на Гаити, многими людьми движет страх. Они боятся неопределённости завтрашнего дня. Боятся, найдут ли еду, работу и одежду. Это противоположно упованию на Бога. В западной культуре люди не боятся таких вещей. Еду и одежду легко найти, рабочих мест много, а медицинскую помощь можно получить, просто позвонив по номеру 911.

Бедные люди здесь, на Гаити, говорят, что им было бы легче доверять Богу, если бы они жили в Америке. Но так ли это на самом деле? Хотя в Америке очень немногие боятся, что им не хватит еды, многие боятся, что их не примут другие люди. Некоторые могут бояться, что им не хватит денег на жизнь, но многие боятся смерти. Каков бы ни был наш страх, ответ — довериться Богу.

Давайте посмотрим на жизнь Давида. Давид был мальчиком. Когда его старшие братья отправились на войну, юный Давид пошёл пасти овец своего отца. На поле битвы вместе с филистимским войском был великан по имени Голиаф. Он бросил вызов израильтянам: пусть выйдет один человек и сразится с ним; войско победителя будет властвовать над другой стороной. В 1-й книге Царств 17:10–11 читаем, что Голиаф сказал: …Ныне я поношу воинство Израильское; дайте мне человека, и мы сразимся вдвоём. Услышав эти слова филистимлянина, Саул и все израильтяне пришли в ужас и сильно испугались.

Позже мы читаем, что Иессей, отец Давида, послал его на место сражения отнести немного еды старшим братьям. Давид пришёл на поле боя и услышал, как Голиаф повторяет те же слова. Увидев, что все израильтяне боятся, Давид не мог этого понять. Почему народ Божий боялся этого необрезанного филистимлянина?

Хотя Давид был молод, он был далеко не новичком в уповании на Бога. Пока он пас овец отца, он, вероятно, много разговаривал с Богом и просил Его помочь уберечь овец. Однажды на овец напал медведь, и Давид убил его. В другой день лев пришёл пожрать овец. И снова юный, бесстрашный, уповающий на Бога Давид встретился с опасностью и убил льва. Теперь, перед лицом, казалось бы, ещё большей опасности, Давид просто спрашивает: …кто этот необрезанный Филистимлянин, что так поносит воинство Бога живого? —1Sa 17:26. Давид пришёл к царю Саулу и сказал: Я …пойду и сражусь с этим Филистимлянином. —1Sa 17:32. Снова уповая на Бога, Давид взял пять гладких камней, побежал навстречу великану и убил его. Увидев такой неожиданный поворот событий, люди изумились.

Согласно Псалму 19:8, уповая на коней и колесницы, мы не уповаем на Господа, Бога нашего. В Евангелии от Матфея 21:21 сказано, что верой мы можем передвигать горы. Здесь, на Гаити, я оказывался в трудных обстоятельствах, когда Бог был для меня единственной надеждой. Когда мне приходилось уповать на Бога, я убеждался, что Он и сейчас творит чудеса. Как Давид, победивший льва, медведя и великана, и мы можем понять, что уповать на Бога всем сердцем — лучший путь, а не просто последнее средство. Когда мы прежде всего уповаем на Господа, мы показываем миру нечто удивительное: Бог, Которому мы служим, жив и реален.

Здесь, на Гаити, один человек жил с женой и тремя маленькими детьми в лачуге высоко в горах. Но была проблема: он был смертельно болен. Однажды он услышал о миссионере, который часто путешествовал по горам. Я получил от него сообщение: он был при смерти и просил меня прийти и помолиться за него. Я поспешил к нему домой. Его состояние поразило меня. Он, вероятно, весил немногим больше 70 фунтов. Жена рассказала, что он уже больше года не вставал с постели. Он не мог говорить, только шептал, тяжело и мучительно дыша. Мы довольно долго говорили о его жизни, его грехе и его будущем. Он сказал, что если Бог исцелит его, то он будет служить Ему и доверять Ему до конца жизни. Я верил в его искренность, но боялся. Я начал молиться, однако это была вовсе не исполненная веры сильная молитва. Скорее это был слабый, смиренный вопль.

По дороге домой и всю ту ночь я не мог думать ни о чём, кроме него. Дьявол начал нападать. Меня одолевали тревожные, сбивающие с толку мысли: «Ты сделал всё, что мог? А если он умрёт? Почему ты не отвёз его в больницу?» Я обратился к Богу в молитве. «О Боже, — молился я, — этот человек просил помолиться за него. Он не просил больницу, не просил лекарств. Прошу Тебя, Боже, исцели его. Если он умрёт, что я буду делать в следующий раз? Отец, если не ради него, то, пожалуйста, исцели его ради меня. Отец, мне нужно, чтобы Ты это сделал».

Я молился так, как никогда прежде, и тогда Бог даровал мне мир. На следующее утро я поспешил вверх по горе к его дому, но его там не было. «Нет, Господи!» — подумал я. Я бросился искать его и заглянул в другую лачугу. Увиденное поразило меня. Он сидел там с широкой улыбкой. Жена сказала, что утром он работал в огороде. Она снова и снова повторяла: «Бог исцелил его! Бог исцелил его!» Я никогда не забуду, что чувствовал, спускаясь с той горы. Сердце переполняли радость и благодарность. «Мой Бог жив! Он может всё, что угодно! Он мой Бог!» Я благодарил и прославлял Его, как никогда прежде. «Лев», с которым мне пришлось столкнуться, был повержен, и моя вера росла. Дьявол не хочет, чтобы мы уповали на Бога, потому что, когда мы уповаем на Бога, Он совершает великие дела, и наша вера растёт.

Когда мы уповаем на Бога, мы рискуем: а что, если Бог не вмешается? Мы можем оказаться в неловком положении, а то и хуже: «А вдруг я сделаю шаг веры, а Бог ничего не сделает?» Помните: это не вера, если нам известен исход. Вера — это послушание и вера Слову Божьему, когда мы не знаем, чем всё закончится. Если бы Бог не помог Давиду, Голиаф наверняка убил бы его. Вера Даниила побуждала его продолжать молиться Богу, хотя он знал, что его ждёт львиный ров. Седрах, Мисах и Авденаго настолько уповали на Бога, что сказали царю: даже если Бог решит не избавлять их от огня, они всё равно …не будут служить богам твоим и не поклонятся золотому истукану, которого ты поставил. —Dan 3:18. А ещё был Гедеон с его тремястами воинами. Можно долго перечислять благочестивых людей, которые рисковали жизнью, доказывая, что их Бог жив.

Когда мы делаем шаг веры, уповая на нашего Бога, всегда что-то происходит (иногда сразу, иногда позже; иногда всё понятно, иногда происходящее кажется совершенно необъяснимым с земной точки зрения). И всё же Бог действует, и наша вера растёт. Когда мы по-настоящему верим в Бога, мы будем Ему доверять. Тогда нам гораздо легче делиться с другими вестью Евангелия. Иисус Навин не держал наготове целый парк бульдозеров у Иерихона; так и нам не нужен запасной план, когда мы уповаем на Бога.

Правда, выдающиеся умы и финансовые возможности многих людей в Америке и других развитых странах вытеснили Бога. Большинство материальных дел можно совершить и без Бога. Более того, большинство людей говорят, что уповать на Бога — неразумно. Если вы молитесь о больном ребёнке, это неразумно. Если вы отказываетесь от высокооплачиваемой работы, потому что не верите, что такова воля Божья, это неразумно. Если вы продаёте своё имущество и раздаёте деньги бедным, это неразумно. Эти люди правы: уповать на Бога неразумно. Обходить стену семь раз, веря, что она рухнет, — неразумно. Идти в бой всего с тремястами воинами против великого войска, которое было числом, как саранча, — тоже неразумно. Многое из того, что делают христиане, уповающие на Бога, кажется бессмысленным, но это показывает миру, что они действительно доверяют Богу. Именно это и перевернёт мир вверх дном вновь — сегодня.

Я хорошо помню один день. Я был далеко от дома, когда мне позвонила жена. Она сказала, чтобы я немедленно возвращался: случилась беда! Нашего двухлетнего сына покусали пчёлы. Я поспешил домой и увидел, что весь район охвачен суматохой. Люди бегали повсюду. Я нашёл жену и сына у соседей — в доме местного пастора. Сын лежал на руках у жены, и она сказала, что его ужалили несколько сотен раз. Пастор с серьёзным видом сказал мне: если я немедленно не отвезу мальчика в больницу, он наверняка умрёт. Я помню, что подумал только одно: Бог может исцелить! Я взял сына и отнёс его через улицу к нам домой и помолился. Вскоре ему стало лучше; уже на следующий день он снова играл на улице.

Многие люди здесь, на Гаити, несут больных к знахарю, и тот их исцеляет. Так здесь бывает. Тем более многое может наш Бог! Пожалуйста, не поймите меня неправильно. Я не говорю, что не следует обращаться к врачу или ехать в больницу; я лишь хочу подчеркнуть, что уповать мы должны на Бога.

Много лет назад я решил подрабатывать продажей ножей. Мне нужно было брать эти ножи и ходить от дома к дому. Ножи меня не интересовали; я просто хотел немного подзаработать. Продавец из меня был ужасный. Куда бы я ни приходил, все отказывались.

Однажды начальник пригласил меня к себе в кабинет и сказал, что заметил: я не продаю ни одного ножа, и понял, что забыл показать мне, как они работают. Мы сидели в его кабинете, а он рассказывал о каждом ноже. У него была небольшая кучка кухонных принадлежностей другой марки, славившихся своим качеством; он использовал их для сравнения. Сначала он поднял небольшой кусок кожи и предложил разрезать его пополам одним из «других» ножей. Я довольно легко перепилил кусок кожи. Затем он велел мне сделать то же самое одним из его ножей. Новый нож рассёк кожу, словно её и не было! Я был по-настоящему поражён. Потом он взял монету в один цент и предложил мне разрезать её пополам «другими» ножницами. Я попробовал, но ничего не вышло: они просто не могли её разрезать. Тогда он велел сделать то же самое его ножницами. Они без труда разрезали монету, и я снова был поражён товаром. Он сказал, что теперь я знаю: эти ножи лучшие, и отныне должен уметь их продавать. Он был прав. Я начал продавать ножи повсюду! Помню, как однажды зашёл в неухоженный трейлер, почти не надеясь, что там что-нибудь купят. К моему удивлению, они купили ножей более чем на 3000 долларов.

Причина, по которой я начал продавать, очевидна: я верил в свой товар. Так и мы, если уповаем на Бога, будем уверены в Нём. В наше время многие, кто называет себя христианами, стыдятся Бога и стыдятся отстаивать истину; мы же можем быть ярким светом. Мы можем идти в мир и в наши общины с Евангелием, в которое действительно верим! Когда мы так поступаем, мир это видит и откликается. Многие ищут, они хотят найти ответы. Когда кто-то спрашивает нас, почему мы поступаем так или иначе или носим ту или иную одежду, что мы отвечаем? Уверенно ли мы отвечаем? Готовы ли привести стих из Библии? Или смущаемся и хотим провалиться сквозь землю? Если бы мир увидел, что мы уверены в нашем Боге и с воодушевлением повинуемся Ему, это стало бы сильным свидетельством.

Помню, как однажды я ехал с небольшой группой через аэропорт. Мы стояли в очереди, и я услышал, как одна женщина спросила одну из незамужних сестёр нашей группы, почему она носит на голове эту «штуку». Я с интересом слушал, стараясь не выдать себя, и обрадовался, услышав её ответ: «Вы когда-нибудь читали 1-е послание к Коринфянам, 11-ю главу? Там сказано, что женщины должны покрывать голову. Это знак покорности». Женщина была поражена ответом и сказала, что никогда раньше об этом не слышала, хотя её отец был пастором. Они продолжили очень интересный разговор, в конце которого женщина захотела вернуться домой и изучить свою Библию.

Брошюра может принести много пользы; то же самое можно сказать о сильной проповеди или печатной статье. Но именно человека, всецело уповающего на Бога, ищет этот мир! Люди хотят «увидеть, что это работает» — и почему бы и нет? Наш Бог хочет явить через нас Свою силу. Несомненно, каждый из нас хочет быть полезным Богу. И каждый из нас может. Ответ в том, чтобы уповать на Господа всем сердцем твоим и не полагаться на разум твой. —Pro 3:5.

If we step back and look at our own life, can we honestly say that we trust in the Lord with all our heart? I often think of my children—they trust in me with all their hearts; there is no fear within them; they do not worry. My prayer is that I can trust in my Heavenly Father in the same way.

Here in Haiti a lot of people are driven by fear. They fear the uncertainty of tomorrow. They fear whether they will find food, work, and clothing. It is the opposite of trusting in God. In the western culture, people don’t fear those things. Food and clothing are easy to find, jobs are plentiful, and medical assistance is just one 911 call away.

The poor people here in Haiti say that it would be easier to trust God if they were in America, but is that truly the case? While very few in America fear whether they will have enough to eat, many fear whether they will be accepted by other people. There are some who may fear having enough money to live, but there are many who fear death. Whatever our fear is, trusting in God is our answer.

Let’s look at the life of David. David was a young boy. When his older brothers went to battle, young David went out to feed his father’s sheep. On the battlefield, there was a giant with the Philistine army named Goliath. He challenged the Israelites by saying that if one man would come out and fight him, the victor’s army would rule the other side. In 1 Samuel 17:10-11 we read that Goliath said, …I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together. When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.

Later on, we read that Jesse, David’s father, sent him to the place of battle to take some food to his older brothers. David arrived at the place of battle, and he heard Goliath speaking these same words. When David saw that the men of Israel were all afraid, he did not understand. Why were God’s people afraid of this uncircumcised Philistine?

Even though David was young, he was no amateur when it came to putting his trust in God. While he was watching his father’s sheep, most likely he talked much with God, asking Him to help guard the sheep. One day a bear came out to attack the sheep, and David killed the bear. Another day a lion came out to eat some sheep. Again, the God-trusting, fearless youth faced the threat and killed the lion. Now, facing a seemingly greater threat, David simply asks, …who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God? –1Sa 17:26. David went to King Saul and said, I …will go and fight with this Philistine –1Sa 17:32. Once more putting his trust in his God, David took five smooth stones, ran out to meet the giant, and killed him. Upon seeing this sudden turn of events, the people marveled.

According to Psalm 20:7, when we put our trust in horses and chariots, then it is not in the Lord our God. In Matthew 21:21, the Bible says that with faith we can move mountains. Here in Haiti I have found myself in tough situations where God is my only option. When I have been forced to put my trust in God, I have discovered that He still works miracles. Just like David with the lion, the bear, and the giant, we too can learn that trusting God with our whole heart is the best way and not just a last resort. When we trust in the Lord first, we show the world something amazing—that this God we serve is alive, and that He is real.

Here in Haiti there was a man living in a shack up in the mountains with his wife and three young children. But there was a problem—he was deathly ill. One day he heard about a missionary who often traveled through the mountains. I received a message from him stating that he was almost dead and that he needed me to come and pray for him. I quickly went up to his home. I was amazed at his condition. His weight was probably not much more than 70 pounds. His wife told me that he had been in bed for over a year. He couldn’t talk, he only whispered with deep agonizing breaths. We spent quite a while discussing his life, his sin, and his future. He told me that if God would heal him, he would serve him and trust him for the rest of his life. I believed his sincerity, yet I was scared. I began to pray, but it was certainly not a powerful prayer full of faith. Rather it was a weak, humble cry.

As I went home and throughout that night, he was all I could think about. The devil began his attack. I had many confusing, troubling thoughts, “Did you do everything you could have done? What if he dies? Why didn’t you take him to the hospital?” I went to God in prayer. “Oh God,” I prayed, “this man wanted prayer. He didn’t ask for a hospital; he didn’t ask for medication. Please God, heal this man. If he dies, what will I do the next time? O Father, if not for him, please, heal him for me. I need you to, Father.”

I prayed like I had never prayed before, and then, God gave me peace. The next morning, I hurried up the mountain to his home, but he wasn’t there. “No, Lord!” I thought. I rushed around and poked my head in another shack. What I saw overwhelmed me. He was sitting there with a big smile on his face. His wife said that he had been working in the garden that morning. Repeatedly she said, “God healed him! God healed him!” I’ll never forget the feeling I had as I travelled back down that mountain. My heart welled up with joy and thankfulness. “My God is alive! He can do anything and everything! He is my God!” I thanked and praised Him like I never had before. “The lion” that I had faced was dead, and my faith was growing. The devil doesn’t want us to trust God, because when we put our trust in God, He does big things, and our faith grows.

When we put our trust in God there is a risk—what if God doesn’t work? We could be embarrassed, or worse—“What if I step out in faith and God does nothing?” Remember, it is not faith if we know the outcome. Faith is walking in obedience and believing God’s Word when we do not know the outcome. If God wouldn’t have helped David, Goliath surely would have killed him. It was Daniel’s faith that kept him praying to God, even though he knew a lion’s den awaited him. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego had so much faith in God that they told the king that even if God chose to not deliver them from the fire, that they still would …not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up –Dan 3:18. Then there was Gideon and his three hundred men. The list goes on and on of godly men who put their life on the line, proving that their God was alive.

When we step out in faith, trusting our God, something always happens (sometimes now, sometimes later; sometimes in a way that makes sense, sometimes in a way that seems to make no earthly sense). Yet God does work, and our faith grows. When we truly believe in God, we will trust him. Then, sharing the Gospel message with others is much easier. Just like Joshua did not have a fleet of bulldozers on standby at Jericho, so also we do not need a backup plan when we trust in God.

It is true that the great minds and financial backing of many in America and other modern countries have replaced God. There is a way to do most physical things without God. In fact, most people say that trusting in God is not common sense. If you pray over a sick child, it’s not common sense. If you turn down a high paying job because you don’t believe that it’s God’s will, that’s not common sense. If you sell your possessions and give to the poor, it’s not common sense. These people are right—trusting in God is not common sense. Marching around a wall seven times, believing it will fall down, is not common sense. Going into battle with only 300 men against a great army who were like grasshoppers for multitude is not common sense either. Most things done by God-trusting Christians don’t make sense, but they do show the world that they really do put their trust in God, and that is what will turn the world upside down again, today.

I remember one day very well. I was away from home when I received a phone call from my wife. She told me to come home quickly—it was an emergency! Our two-year-old son had been stung by bees. I rushed home to see the neighborhood in chaos. People where running around everywhere. I found my wife and son at the neighbor’s house, a local pastor. My son lay in the arms of my wife who told me he had been stung several hundred times. The pastor looked at me quite gravely, telling me that if I didn’t get this boy to a hospital right away, he would surely die. I remember thinking one thing—God can heal! I picked up my son and took him across the street to our house, and I prayed. It didn’t take long before he began to recover—by the next day he was back out playing.

Many people here in Haiti take their sick to the witch doctor, and he heals them. It’s just what happens. How much more can our God do! Please don’t misunderstand me. I’m not saying we shouldn’t go to the medical doctor or to the hospital; rather, I’m trying to emphasize that our trust should be in God.

Years ago, I decided to take up a part-time job selling knives. I was to take these knives and travel from home to home. I didn’t have an interest in knives but was just trying to make some extra money. I was a terrible knife salesman. Everywhere I went everyone said no.

One day the boss took me into his office where he told me that he had noticed I wasn’t selling any knives and realized he had forgotten to show me how the knives worked. So, we sat there in his office as he talked about each knife. He had a small pile of kitchen utensils of another brand, which were known for their quality, that he used for a comparison. First, he held up a small piece of leather and asked me to cut it in half with one of the “other” knives. I sawed through the piece of leather with some ease. Then he instructed me to use one of his knives and do the same thing. The new knife sliced through the leather as if it wasn’t even there! I was truly amazed. He then picked up a penny and told me to cut it in half using the “other” scissors. I tried but failed; they simply would not cut it. He then told me to do the same using his scissors. It easily cut through the penny, and again I was amazed at the product. He told me that I now knew that these knives were the best and from now on I should be able to sell them. He was right. I began selling knives everywhere I went! I even remember walking into a poorly kept trailer home without much hope that they would buy. Surprisingly, they bought over $3,000 worth of knives.

The reason I began to make sales is obvious—I believed in my product. Likewise, if we put our trust in God, we will have confidence. In a day when most proclaiming Christians are ashamed of God and ashamed to stand up for truth, we can be a bright and shining light. We can be a people who go out into the world and into our communities with a Gospel that we truly believe in! As we do, the world will see it and respond. Many are seeking; they are looking for answers. When someone asks us a question about why we do the things we do or wear what we wear, what is our reply? Do we reply with confidence? Do we have a ready Bible verse? Or do we get embarrassed and desire a hole to climb into? If the world could see that we are confident in our God, and that we obey him with enthusiasm, it would be a powerful testimony.

I remember traveling through the airport with a small group. As we were standing in line, I overheard a lady ask one of the single sisters in our group why she wore that “thing” on her head. I was excited to listen unnoticed, and I rejoiced as I heard her response. “Have you ever read 1 Corinthians 11? There it instructs us that women should cover their heads. It’s a sign of submission.” The woman was shocked at her answer, saying she never heard that before, and that her father was a pastor. They continued to have a very interesting conversation that ended with that lady desiring to go home and study her Bible.

A tract can do a lot of good; so likewise, a powerful sermon or a printed article, but someone putting all his trust in God is what this world is looking for! They want to “see something that works,” and why not? Our God wants to use us to show Himself strong. Surely each one of us wants to be used by God. We can. Each one of us can. The answer is to trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding –Pro 3:5.

Als we een stap terugdoen en naar ons eigen leven kijken, kunnen we dan eerlijk zeggen dat we met heel ons hart op de Heer vertrouwen? Ik denk vaak aan mijn kinderen: zij vertrouwen met heel hun hart op mij; ze zijn niet bang en maken zich geen zorgen. Mijn gebed is dat ik op dezelfde manier op mijn hemelse Vader kan vertrouwen.

Hier in Haïti worden veel mensen door angst gedreven. Ze zijn bang voor de onzekerheid van morgen. Ze zijn bang of ze voedsel, werk en kleding zullen vinden. Dat is het tegenovergestelde van op God vertrouwen. In de westerse cultuur zijn mensen daar niet bang voor. Voedsel en kleding zijn gemakkelijk te vinden, er is volop werk en medische hulp is slechts één telefoontje naar 911 verwijderd.

De arme mensen hier in Haïti zeggen dat het gemakkelijker zou zijn om op God te vertrouwen als ze in Amerika waren, maar is dat echt zo? Hoewel maar heel weinig mensen in Amerika bang zijn dat ze niet genoeg te eten zullen hebben, zijn velen bang of andere mensen hen zullen accepteren. Sommigen zijn misschien bang dat ze niet genoeg geld zullen hebben om van te leven, maar velen zijn bang voor de dood. Wat onze angst ook is, op God vertrouwen is het antwoord.

Laten we eens kijken naar het leven van David. David was een jonge jongen. Toen zijn oudere broers ten strijde trokken, ging de jonge David eropuit om de schapen van zijn vader te hoeden. Op het slagveld was er een reus bij het Filistijnse leger, Goliat genaamd. Hij daagde de Israëlieten uit door te zeggen dat als één man naar voren zou komen om met hem te vechten, het leger van de overwinnaar over de andere partij zou heersen. In 1 Samuël 17:10-11 lezen we dat Goliat zei: …Ik daag vandaag de legers van Israël uit; geef mij een man, zodat wij met elkaar kunnen vechten. Toen Saul en heel Israël die woorden van de Filistijn hoorden, waren zij ontsteld en zeer bevreesd.

Later lezen we dat Isaï, Davids vader, hem naar het slagveld stuurde om wat voedsel naar zijn oudere broers te brengen. David kwam aan op het slagveld en hoorde Goliat dezelfde woorden spreken. Toen David zag dat de mannen van Israël allemaal bang waren, begreep hij het niet. Waarom waren Gods volk bang voor deze onbesneden Filistijn?

Hoewel David jong was, was hij geen beginner in het vertrouwen op God. Terwijl hij de schapen van zijn vader hoedde, sprak hij waarschijnlijk veel met God en vroeg Hem om de schapen te beschermen. Op een dag kwam er een beer op de schapen af, en David doodde de beer. Een andere dag kwam er een leeuw om enkele schapen op te eten. Opnieuw ging de jeugdige, op God vertrouwende en onverschrokken David de dreiging tegemoet en doodde de leeuw. Nu hij tegenover een schijnbaar nog grotere dreiging staat, vraagt David eenvoudig: …wie is deze onbesneden Filistijn, dat hij de legers van de levende God uitdaagt? –1Sa 17:26. David ging naar koning Saul en zei: Ik …zal gaan en met deze Filistijn vechten –1Sa 17:32. Opnieuw vertrouwend op zijn God nam David vijf gladde stenen, rende de reus tegemoet en doodde hem. Toen de mensen deze plotselinge wending zagen, stonden ze versteld.

Volgens Psalm 20:7 vertrouwen we, wanneer we op paarden en strijdwagens vertrouwen, niet op de HEER, onze God. In Mattheüs 21:21 zegt de Bijbel dat we met geloof bergen kunnen verzetten. Hier in Haïti ben ik in moeilijke situaties terechtgekomen waarin God mijn enige mogelijkheid was. Wanneer ik gedwongen werd op God te vertrouwen, ontdekte ik dat Hij nog steeds wonderen doet. Net als David met de leeuw, de beer en de reus kunnen ook wij leren dat met heel ons hart op God vertrouwen de beste manier is en niet slechts een laatste redmiddel. Wanneer we eerst op de Heer vertrouwen, laten we de wereld iets verbazingwekkends zien: dat de God die wij dienen leeft en echt is.

Hier in Haïti woonde een man met zijn vrouw en drie jonge kinderen in een hut hoog in de bergen. Maar er was een probleem: hij was doodziek. Op een dag hoorde hij over een zendeling die vaak door de bergen reisde. Ik ontving een bericht van hem waarin stond dat hij bijna dood was en dat hij wilde dat ik naar hem toe kwam om voor hem te bidden. Ik ging snel naar zijn huis. Ik was verbaasd over zijn toestand. Hij woog waarschijnlijk niet veel meer dan 70 pond. Zijn vrouw vertelde me dat hij al meer dan een jaar in bed lag. Hij kon niet praten, hij fluisterde alleen met diepe, pijnlijke ademhalingen. We spraken geruime tijd over zijn leven, zijn zonde en zijn toekomst. Hij vertelde me dat hij God zou dienen en de rest van zijn leven op Hem zou vertrouwen als God hem zou genezen. Ik geloofde dat hij oprecht was, maar toch was ik bang. Ik begon te bidden, maar het was beslist geen krachtig gebed vol geloof. Het was eerder een zwakke, nederige smeekbede.

Toen ik naar huis ging en gedurende die nacht kon ik alleen maar aan hem denken. De duivel begon zijn aanval. Ik had allerlei verwarrende, verontrustende gedachten: ‘Heb je alles gedaan wat je had kunnen doen? Wat als hij sterft? Waarom heb je hem niet naar het ziekenhuis gebracht?’ Ik ging in gebed tot God. ‘O God,’ bad ik, ‘deze man wilde dat er voor hem gebeden werd. Hij vroeg niet om een ziekenhuis; hij vroeg niet om medicijnen. Alstublieft, God, genees deze man. Als hij sterft, wat moet ik dan de volgende keer doen? O Vader, al was het maar voor mij, genees hem alstublieft. Vader, ik heb U nodig.’

Ik bad zoals ik nog nooit eerder had gebeden, en toen gaf God mij vrede. De volgende ochtend haastte ik me de berg op naar zijn huis, maar hij was er niet. ‘Nee, Heer!’ dacht ik. Ik rende rond en stak mijn hoofd in een andere hut. Wat ik zag, overweldigde me. Hij zat daar met een brede glimlach op zijn gezicht. Zijn vrouw zei dat hij die ochtend in de tuin had gewerkt. Steeds weer zei ze: ‘God heeft hem genezen! God heeft hem genezen!’ Ik zal nooit vergeten hoe ik me voelde toen ik weer de berg afliep. Mijn hart liep over van vreugde en dankbaarheid. ‘Mijn God leeft! Hij kan alles en nog wat doen! Hij is mijn God!’ Ik dankte en prees Hem zoals ik dat nog nooit eerder had gedaan. ‘De leeuw’ waar ik tegenover had gestaan, was dood, en mijn geloof groeide. De duivel wil niet dat we op God vertrouwen, want wanneer we op God vertrouwen, doet Hij grote dingen en groeit ons geloof.

Wanneer we op God vertrouwen, nemen we een risico: wat als God niet ingrijpt? We zouden ons kunnen schamen, of erger: ‘Wat als ik in geloof een stap zet en God niets doet?’ Bedenk dat het geen geloof is als we de uitkomst kennen. Geloof is gehoorzaam wandelen en Gods Woord geloven wanneer we de uitkomst niet kennen. Als God David niet geholpen had, zou Goliat hem zeker hebben gedood. Het was Daniels geloof dat hem ertoe bracht tot God te blijven bidden, hoewel hij wist dat de leeuwenkuil op hem wachtte. Sadrach, Mesach en Abednego hadden zo’n groot geloof in God dat ze tegen de koning zeiden dat ze, zelfs als God ervoor koos hen niet uit het vuur te redden, …uw goden niet zullen dienen en het gouden beeld dat u hebt opgericht niet zullen aanbidden –Dan 3:18. En dan was er Gideon met zijn driehonderd mannen. De lijst van godvrezende mannen die hun leven op het spel zetten om te bewijzen dat hun God leeft, gaat maar door.

Wanneer we in geloof naar voren stappen en op onze God vertrouwen, gebeurt er altijd iets (soms nu, soms later; soms op een manier die begrijpelijk is, soms op een manier die geen enkele aardse verklaring lijkt te hebben). Toch handelt God, en groeit ons geloof. Wanneer we echt in God geloven, zullen we op Hem vertrouwen. Dan wordt het veel gemakkelijker om de evangelieboodschap met anderen te delen. Net zoals Jozua bij Jericho geen vloot bulldozers stand-by had staan, hebben ook wij geen reserveplan nodig wanneer we op God vertrouwen.

Het is waar dat de grote denkers en de financiële steun van velen in Amerika en andere moderne landen God hebben vervangen. De meeste praktische dingen kunnen op een manier zonder God worden gedaan. In feite zeggen de meeste mensen dat op God vertrouwen geen gezond verstand is. Als je voor een ziek kind bidt, is dat geen gezond verstand. Als je een goedbetaalde baan afslaat omdat je niet gelooft dat het Gods wil is, is dat geen gezond verstand. Als je je bezittingen verkoopt en aan de armen geeft, is dat geen gezond verstand. Deze mensen hebben gelijk: op God vertrouwen is geen gezond verstand. Zeven keer rond een muur lopen in de overtuiging dat die zal instorten, is geen gezond verstand. De strijd aangaan met slechts 300 mannen tegenover een groot leger, dat talrijk was als sprinkhanen, is evenmin gezond verstand. De meeste dingen die door christenen worden gedaan die op God vertrouwen, zijn niet logisch, maar ze laten de wereld wel zien dat zij werkelijk op God vertrouwen, en dat is wat de wereld vandaag opnieuw op zijn kop zal zetten.

Ik herinner me één dag nog heel goed. Ik was niet thuis toen ik een telefoontje van mijn vrouw kreeg. Ze zei dat ik snel naar huis moest komen: het was een noodgeval! Onze tweejarige zoon was door bijen gestoken. Ik haastte me naar huis en zag dat de buurt in rep en roer was. Overal renden mensen rond. Ik vond mijn vrouw en zoon bij het huis van de buurman, een plaatselijke predikant. Mijn zoon lag in de armen van mijn vrouw, die me vertelde dat hij honderden keren was gestoken. De predikant keek me ernstig aan en zei dat mijn zoon zeker zou sterven als ik hem niet meteen naar een ziekenhuis bracht. Ik herinner me dat ik één ding dacht: God kan genezen! Ik tilde mijn zoon op, bracht hem naar ons huis aan de overkant van de straat en bad. Het duurde niet lang voordat hij begon op te knappen; de volgende dag speelde hij alweer buiten.

Veel mensen hier in Haïti brengen hun zieken naar de toverdokter, en hij geneest hen. Zo gaat dat nu eenmaal. Hoeveel te meer kan onze God doen! Begrijp me alstublieft niet verkeerd. Ik zeg niet dat we niet naar de arts of naar het ziekenhuis moeten gaan; ik probeer juist te benadrukken dat ons vertrouwen op God moet zijn gevestigd.

Jaren geleden besloot ik er een parttimebaan bij te nemen als messenverkoper. Ik moest met die messen van huis naar huis reizen. Ik had geen belangstelling voor messen, maar probeerde gewoon wat extra geld te verdienen. Ik was een vreselijke messenverkoper. Overal waar ik kwam, zei iedereen nee.

Op een dag nam mijn baas me mee naar zijn kantoor. Hij vertelde me dat hij had gemerkt dat ik geen messen verkocht en besefte dat hij vergeten was me te laten zien hoe de messen werkten. Dus zaten we daar in zijn kantoor terwijl hij over elk mes vertelde. Hij had een klein stapeltje keukenbenodigdheden van een ander merk, dat bekendstond om zijn kwaliteit, om mee te vergelijken. Eerst hield hij een klein stukje leer omhoog en vroeg me het met een van de ‘andere’ messen doormidden te snijden. Ik zaagde het stukje leer er vrij gemakkelijk doorheen. Daarna zei hij dat ik hetzelfde met een van zijn messen moest doen. Het nieuwe mes sneed door het leer alsof het er niet eens was! Ik was werkelijk verbaasd. Daarna pakte hij een penny en zei dat ik die met de ‘andere’ schaar moest doorknippen. Ik probeerde het, maar het lukte niet; de schaar wilde er gewoon niet doorheen. Toen zei hij dat ik hetzelfde met zijn schaar moest doen. Die knipte de penny met gemak door, en opnieuw was ik verbaasd over het product. Hij zei dat ik nu wist dat deze messen de beste waren en ze voortaan moest kunnen verkopen. Hij had gelijk. Ik begon overal waar ik kwam messen te verkopen! Ik herinner me zelfs dat ik een slecht onderhouden stacaravan binnenliep, zonder veel hoop dat ze iets zouden kopen. Tot mijn verbazing kochten ze voor meer dan $3.000 aan messen.

De reden waarom ik verkopen begon te maken, is duidelijk: ik geloofde in mijn product. Zo zullen ook wij vertrouwen hebben als we op God vertrouwen. In een tijd waarin de meeste christenen die belijden christen te zijn zich voor God schamen en ervoor terugdeinzen voor de waarheid op te komen, kunnen wij een helder schijnend licht zijn. Wij kunnen een volk zijn dat de wereld en onze gemeenschappen ingaat met een evangelie waarin we echt geloven! Als we dat doen, zal de wereld het zien en reageren. Velen zijn op zoek; ze zoeken naar antwoorden. Als iemand ons vraagt waarom we de dingen doen die we doen of dragen wat we dragen, wat antwoorden we dan? Antwoorden we vol vertrouwen? Hebben we een Bijbelvers paraat? Of schamen we ons en zouden we het liefst in een gat kruipen? Als de wereld kon zien dat we vertrouwen hebben in onze God en Hem enthousiast gehoorzamen, zou dat een krachtig getuigenis zijn.

Ik herinner me dat ik met een klein groepje door de luchthaven reisde. Terwijl we in de rij stonden, hoorde ik een vrouw aan een van de ongetrouwde zusters in onze groep vragen waarom ze dat ‘ding’ op haar hoofd droeg. Ik vond het spannend om ongemerkt te luisteren en was blij toen ik haar antwoord hoorde: ‘Hebt u weleens 1 Korinthe 11 gelezen? Daar staat dat vrouwen hun hoofd moeten bedekken. Het is een teken van onderwerping.’ De vrouw was verbaasd over haar antwoord en zei dat ze daar nog nooit van had gehoord en dat haar vader predikant was. Ze bleven een heel interessant gesprek voeren, dat eindigde met haar verlangen om naar huis te gaan en haar Bijbel te bestuderen.

Een traktaat kan veel goeds doen, en dat geldt ook voor een krachtige preek of een gedrukt artikel, maar deze wereld is op zoek naar iemand die met heel zijn vertrouwen op God vertrouwt! Ze willen ‘zien dat iets werkt’, en waarom ook niet? Onze God wil ons gebruiken om te laten zien hoe machtig Hij is. Ieder van ons wil toch door God gebruikt worden? Dat kan. Ieder van ons kan dat. Het antwoord is: Vertrouw op de HEER met heel uw hart en steun niet op uw eigen inzicht –Spr 3:5.
