Αν κάνουμε ένα βήμα πίσω και κοιτάξουμε τη δική μας ζωή, μπορούμε άραγε να πούμε με ειλικρίνεια ότι εμπιστευόμαστε τον Κύριο με όλη μας την καρδιά; Συχνά σκέφτομαι τα παιδιά μου—με εμπιστεύονται με όλη τους την καρδιά· δεν φοβούνται καθόλου· δεν ανησυχούν. Προσεύχομαι να μπορώ κι εγώ να εμπιστεύομαι τον ουράνιο Πατέρα μου με τον ίδιο τρόπο.

Εδώ στην Αϊτή πολλοί άνθρωποι κυριαρχούνται από τον φόβο. Φοβούνται την αβεβαιότητα του αύριο. Φοβούνται μήπως δεν βρουν τροφή, δουλειά και ρούχα. Αυτό είναι το αντίθετο της εμπιστοσύνης στον Θεό. Στη δυτική κουλτούρα οι άνθρωποι δεν φοβούνται αυτά τα πράγματα. Η τροφή και τα ρούχα βρίσκονται εύκολα, υπάρχουν πολλές διαθέσιμες θέσεις εργασίας και η ιατρική βοήθεια απέχει μόλις ένα τηλεφώνημα στο 911.

Οι φτωχοί άνθρωποι εδώ στην Αϊτή λένε πως θα ήταν ευκολότερο να εμπιστεύονται τον Θεό αν ζούσαν στην Αμερική, αλλά ισχύει πράγματι αυτό; Ενώ ελάχιστοι στην Αμερική φοβούνται μήπως δεν έχουν αρκετό φαγητό, πολλοί φοβούνται μήπως δεν γίνουν αποδεκτοί από τους άλλους. Κάποιοι ίσως φοβούνται μήπως δεν έχουν αρκετά χρήματα για να ζήσουν, αλλά πολλοί φοβούνται τον θάνατο. Όποιος κι αν είναι ο φόβος μας, η απάντηση είναι να εμπιστευόμαστε τον Θεό.

Ας δούμε τη ζωή του Δαβίδ. Ο Δαβίδ ήταν ένα νεαρό αγόρι. Όταν οι μεγαλύτεροι αδελφοί του πήγαν στον πόλεμο, ο νεαρός Δαβίδ πήγε να βόσκει τα πρόβατα του πατέρα του. Στο πεδίο της μάχης, με τον στρατό των Φιλισταίων, υπήρχε ένας γίγαντας ονόματι Γολιάθ. Προκάλεσε τους Ισραηλίτες λέγοντας πως, αν έβγαινε ένας άντρας να τον πολεμήσει, ο στρατός του νικητή θα εξουσίαζε την άλλη πλευρά. Στο Α΄ Σαμουήλ 17:10-11 διαβάζουμε ότι ο Γολιάθ είπε: …Εγώ σήμερα αψηφώ τα στρατεύματα του Ισραήλ· δώστε μου έναν άντρα να πολεμήσουμε. Όταν ο Σαούλ και όλος ο Ισραήλ άκουσαν αυτά τα λόγια του Φιλισταίου, ταράχτηκαν και φοβήθηκαν πάρα πολύ.

Αργότερα διαβάζουμε πως ο Ιεσσαί, ο πατέρας του Δαβίδ, τον έστειλε στο πεδίο της μάχης για να πάει λίγο φαγητό στους μεγαλύτερους αδελφούς του. Ο Δαβίδ έφτασε στο πεδίο της μάχης και άκουσε τον Γολιάθ να λέει τα ίδια λόγια. Όταν ο Δαβίδ είδε πως όλοι οι άντρες του Ισραήλ φοβούνταν, δεν μπορούσε να το καταλάβει. Γιατί φοβόταν ο λαός του Θεού αυτόν τον απερίτμητο Φιλισταίο;

Παρόλο που ο Δαβίδ ήταν νέος, δεν ήταν καθόλου άπειρος στο να εμπιστεύεται τον Θεό. Όταν φύλαγε τα πρόβατα του πατέρα του, πιθανότατα μιλούσε συχνά με τον Θεό και Του ζητούσε να τον βοηθά να προστατεύει τα πρόβατα. Μια μέρα βγήκε μια αρκούδα και επιτέθηκε στα πρόβατα, και ο Δαβίδ σκότωσε την αρκούδα. Μια άλλη μέρα βγήκε ένα λιοντάρι για να φάει μερικά πρόβατα. Και πάλι, ο άφοβος νέος που εμπιστευόταν τον Θεό αντιμετώπισε την απειλή και σκότωσε το λιοντάρι. Τώρα, μπροστά σε μια φαινομενικά μεγαλύτερη απειλή, ο Δαβίδ απλώς ρωτά: …ποιος είναι αυτός ο απερίτμητος Φιλισταίος, ώστε να αψηφά τα στρατεύματα του ζωντανού Θεού; –Α΄Σα 17:26. Ο Δαβίδ πήγε στον βασιλιά Σαούλ και είπε: Εγώ …θα πάω να πολεμήσω αυτόν τον Φιλισταίο –Α΄Σα 17:32. Εμπιστευόμενος για άλλη μια φορά τον Θεό του, ο Δαβίδ πήρε πέντε λείες πέτρες, έτρεξε να συναντήσει τον γίγαντα και τον σκότωσε. Βλέποντας αυτή την απρόσμενη τροπή των γεγονότων, ο λαός έμεινε έκπληκτος.

Σύμφωνα με τον Ψαλμό 20:7, όταν εμπιστευόμαστε άλογα και άρματα, τότε δεν εμπιστευόμαστε τον Κύριο τον Θεό μας. Στο Κατά Ματθαίον 21:21, η Βίβλος λέει ότι με πίστη μπορούμε να μετακινήσουμε βουνά. Εδώ στην Αϊτή έχω βρεθεί σε δύσκολες καταστάσεις όπου ο Θεός ήταν η μόνη μου επιλογή. Όταν αναγκάστηκα να εμπιστευτώ τον Θεό, ανακάλυψα ότι εξακολουθεί να κάνει θαύματα. Όπως ο Δαβίδ με το λιοντάρι, την αρκούδα και τον γίγαντα, έτσι κι εμείς μπορούμε να μάθουμε ότι το να εμπιστευόμαστε τον Θεό με όλη μας την καρδιά είναι ο καλύτερος δρόμος, κι όχι απλώς η έσχατη λύση. Όταν εμπιστευόμαστε πρώτα τον Κύριο, δείχνουμε στον κόσμο κάτι θαυμαστό—ότι αυτός ο Θεός που υπηρετούμε είναι ζωντανός και αληθινός.

Εδώ στην Αϊτή ζούσε κάποτε ένας άντρας σε μια παράγκα ψηλά στα βουνά, μαζί με τη γυναίκα του και τα τρία μικρά παιδιά τους. Υπήρχε όμως ένα πρόβλημα—ήταν βαριά άρρωστος και κινδύνευε να πεθάνει. Μια μέρα έμαθε για έναν ιεραπόστολο που ταξίδευε συχνά μέσα από τα βουνά. Έλαβα ένα μήνυμα από εκείνον, όπου μου έλεγε ότι ήταν σχεδόν ετοιμοθάνατος και ότι έπρεπε να πάω να προσευχηθώ γι’ αυτόν. Ανέβηκα γρήγορα στο σπίτι του. Η κατάστασή του με άφησε κατάπληκτο. Πιθανότατα δεν ζύγιζε πολύ περισσότερο από 70 λίβρες. Η γυναίκα του μου είπε ότι ήταν κατάκοιτος πάνω από έναν χρόνο. Δεν μπορούσε να μιλήσει· μόνο ψιθύριζε, παίρνοντας βαθιές και βασανιστικές ανάσες. Συζητήσαμε αρκετή ώρα για τη ζωή του, την αμαρτία του και το μέλλον του. Μου είπε πως αν ο Θεός τον θεράπευε, θα Τον υπηρετούσε και θα Τον εμπιστευόταν για το υπόλοιπο της ζωής του. Πίστεψα ότι ήταν ειλικρινής, κι όμως φοβόμουν. Άρχισα να προσεύχομαι, αλλά ασφαλώς δεν ήταν μια δυνατή προσευχή γεμάτη πίστη. Ήταν μάλλον μια αδύναμη, ταπεινή κραυγή.

Καθώς επέστρεφα στο σπίτι και όλη εκείνη τη νύχτα, δεν μπορούσα να σκεφτώ τίποτε άλλο παρά εκείνον. Ο διάβολος άρχισε την επίθεσή του. Πολλές σκέψεις με μπέρδευαν και με βασάνιζαν: «Έκανες ό,τι μπορούσες; Κι αν πεθάνει; Γιατί δεν τον πήγες στο νοσοκομείο;» Προσευχήθηκα στον Θεό. «Ω Θεέ μου», προσευχήθηκα, «αυτός ο άνθρωπος ζήτησε προσευχή. Δεν ζήτησε νοσοκομείο· δεν ζήτησε φάρμακα. Σε παρακαλώ, Θεέ μου, θεράπευσέ τον. Αν πεθάνει, τι θα κάνω την επόμενη φορά; Ω Πατέρα, αν όχι για χάρη του, σε παρακαλώ, θεράπευσέ τον για χάρη μου. Σε χρειάζομαι, Πατέρα».

Προσευχήθηκα όπως δεν είχα προσευχηθεί ποτέ άλλοτε, και τότε ο Θεός μού έδωσε ειρήνη. Το επόμενο πρωί ανέβηκα βιαστικά στο βουνό, στο σπίτι του, αλλά εκείνος δεν ήταν εκεί. «Όχι, Κύριε!» σκέφτηκα. Έτρεξα ολόγυρα και έσκυψα να κοιτάξω μέσα σε μια άλλη παράγκα. Αυτό που είδα με συγκλόνισε. Καθόταν εκεί με ένα πλατύ χαμόγελο. Η γυναίκα του είπε πως εκείνο το πρωί είχε δουλέψει στον κήπο. Επανειλημμένα έλεγε: «Ο Θεός τον θεράπευσε! Ο Θεός τον θεράπευσε!» Δεν θα ξεχάσω ποτέ πώς ένιωθα καθώς κατέβαινα ξανά εκείνο το βουνό. Η καρδιά μου ξεχείλιζε από χαρά και ευγνωμοσύνη. «Ο Θεός μου είναι ζωντανός! Μπορεί να κάνει το καθετί! Είναι ο Θεός μου!» Τον ευχαρίστησα και Τον δόξασα όπως δεν το είχα κάνει ποτέ πριν. «Το λιοντάρι» που είχα αντιμετωπίσει ήταν νεκρό, και η πίστη μου μεγάλωνε. Ο διάβολος δεν θέλει να εμπιστευόμαστε τον Θεό, γιατί όταν εμπιστευόμαστε τον Θεό, Εκείνος κάνει μεγάλα πράγματα και η πίστη μας μεγαλώνει.

Όταν εμπιστευόμαστε τον Θεό, υπάρχει ένας κίνδυνος—κι αν ο Θεός δεν ενεργήσει; Μπορεί να ντροπιαστούμε ή, ακόμη χειρότερα—«Κι αν κάνω ένα βήμα με πίστη και ο Θεός δεν κάνει τίποτε;» Να θυμάστε, δεν είναι πίστη αν ξέρουμε ποιο θα είναι το αποτέλεσμα. Πίστη είναι να υπακούμε και να πιστεύουμε τον λόγο του Θεού όταν δεν ξέρουμε ποιο θα είναι το αποτέλεσμα. Αν ο Θεός δεν βοηθούσε τον Δαβίδ, ο Γολιάθ σίγουρα θα τον σκότωνε. Η πίστη του Δανιήλ ήταν αυτή που τον κράτησε να προσεύχεται στον Θεό, παρόλο που ήξερε πως τον περίμενε ο λάκκος των λιονταριών. Ο Σεδράχ, ο Μισάχ και ο Αβδέ-νεγώ είχαν τόσο μεγάλη πίστη στον Θεό, ώστε είπαν στον βασιλιά πως ακόμη κι αν ο Θεός επέλεγε να μην τους σώσει από τη φωτιά, εκείνοι …δεν θα λατρεύσουμε τους θεούς σου ούτε θα προσκυνήσουμε τη χρυσή εικόνα που έστησες –Δα 3:18. Και ύστερα ήταν ο Γεδεών και οι τριακόσιοι άντρες του. Ο κατάλογος των ευσεβών αντρών που διακινδύνευσαν τη ζωή τους, αποδεικνύοντας πως ο Θεός τους ήταν ζωντανός, συνεχίζεται ατέλειωτα.

Όταν προχωρούμε με πίστη, εμπιστευόμενοι τον Θεό μας, κάτι συμβαίνει πάντα (κάποτε αμέσως, κάποτε αργότερα· κάποτε με τρόπο που βγάζει νόημα, κάποτε με τρόπο που φαίνεται εντελώς παράλογος από ανθρώπινη σκοπιά). Ωστόσο, ο Θεός ενεργεί και η πίστη μας μεγαλώνει. Όταν πιστεύουμε πραγματικά στον Θεό, Τον εμπιστευόμαστε. Τότε είναι πολύ ευκολότερο να μοιραζόμαστε το μήνυμα του Ευαγγελίου με άλλους. Όπως ο Ιησούς του Ναυή δεν είχε έτοιμο έναν στόλο από μπουλντόζες στην Ιεριχώ, έτσι κι εμείς δεν χρειαζόμαστε εναλλακτικό σχέδιο όταν εμπιστευόμαστε τον Θεό.

Είναι αλήθεια ότι τα μεγάλα μυαλά και η οικονομική στήριξη πολλών ανθρώπων στην Αμερική και σε άλλες σύγχρονες χώρες έχουν πάρει τη θέση του Θεού. Υπάρχει τρόπος να γίνουν τα περισσότερα πρακτικά πράγματα χωρίς τον Θεό. Στην πραγματικότητα, οι περισσότεροι λένε ότι η εμπιστοσύνη στον Θεό δεν είναι κοινή λογική. Αν προσευχηθείς για ένα άρρωστο παιδί, αυτό δεν είναι κοινή λογική. Αν αρνηθείς μια καλοπληρωμένη δουλειά επειδή δεν πιστεύεις πως είναι θέλημα του Θεού, αυτό δεν είναι κοινή λογική. Αν πουλήσεις τα υπάρχοντά σου και δώσεις τα χρήματα στους φτωχούς, αυτό δεν είναι κοινή λογική. Αυτοί οι άνθρωποι έχουν δίκιο—η εμπιστοσύνη στον Θεό δεν είναι κοινή λογική. Το να κάνεις επτά φορές τον γύρο ενός τείχους πιστεύοντας πως θα πέσει δεν είναι κοινή λογική. Ούτε είναι κοινή λογική να πας στη μάχη με μόλις 300 άντρες εναντίον ενός μεγάλου στρατού που ήταν σαν ακρίδες στο πλήθος. Τα περισσότερα απ’ όσα κάνουν οι χριστιανοί που εμπιστεύονται τον Θεό δεν βγάζουν νόημα, όμως δείχνουν στον κόσμο ότι πραγματικά εμπιστεύονται τον Θεό, κι αυτό είναι που θα αναποδογυρίσει ξανά τον κόσμο, σήμερα.

Θυμάμαι πολύ καλά μια μέρα. Έλειπα από το σπίτι όταν έλαβα ένα τηλεφώνημα από τη γυναίκα μου. Μου είπε να γυρίσω γρήγορα—ήταν επείγον! Τον δίχρονο γιο μας τον είχαν τσιμπήσει μέλισσες. Έτρεξα σπίτι και είδα τη γειτονιά σε αναστάτωση. Οι άνθρωποι έτρεχαν παντού. Βρήκα τη γυναίκα μου και τον γιο μου στο σπίτι του γείτονα, ενός τοπικού πάστορα. Ο γιος μου ήταν ξαπλωμένος στην αγκαλιά της γυναίκας μου, η οποία μου είπε ότι τον είχαν τσιμπήσει εκατοντάδες φορές. Ο πάστορας με κοίταξε πολύ σοβαρά και μου είπε πως, αν δεν πήγαινα αμέσως το αγόρι στο νοσοκομείο, σίγουρα θα πέθαινε. Θυμάμαι ότι σκέφτηκα ένα πράγμα—ο Θεός μπορεί να θεραπεύσει! Πήρα τον γιο μου και τον πήγα απέναντι, στο σπίτι μας, και προσευχήθηκα. Δεν πέρασε πολύς χρόνος πριν αρχίσει να αναρρώνει—την επόμενη κιόλας μέρα έπαιζε πάλι έξω.

Πολλοί άνθρωποι εδώ στην Αϊτή πηγαίνουν τους αρρώστους τους στον μάγο-γιατρό, και εκείνος τους θεραπεύει. Έτσι γίνεται. Πόσο περισσότερο μπορεί να κάνει ο Θεός μας! Σας παρακαλώ, μην παρεξηγήσετε τα λόγια μου. Δεν λέω ότι δεν πρέπει να πηγαίνουμε στον γιατρό ή στο νοσοκομείο· αντίθετα, προσπαθώ να τονίσω ότι πρέπει να εμπιστευόμαστε τον Θεό.

Πριν από χρόνια αποφάσισα να πιάσω μια δουλειά μερικής απασχόλησης πουλώντας μαχαίρια. Θα έπαιρνα τα μαχαίρια και θα πήγαινα από σπίτι σε σπίτι. Δεν με ενδιέφεραν τα μαχαίρια· απλώς προσπαθούσα να βγάλω λίγα επιπλέον χρήματα. Ήμουν απαίσιος πωλητής μαχαιριών. Όπου κι αν πήγαινα, όλοι έλεγαν όχι.

Μια μέρα το αφεντικό με πήγε στο γραφείο του, όπου μου είπε πως είχε παρατηρήσει ότι δεν πουλούσα καθόλου μαχαίρια και συνειδητοποίησε ότι είχε ξεχάσει να μου δείξει πώς λειτουργούσαν. Καθίσαμε λοιπόν εκεί στο γραφείο του και μου μίλησε για κάθε μαχαίρι. Είχε έναν μικρό σωρό από κουζινικά σκεύη μιας άλλης μάρκας, γνωστής για την ποιότητά της, και τα χρησιμοποιούσε για σύγκριση. Πρώτα σήκωσε ένα μικρό κομμάτι δέρμα και μου ζήτησε να το κόψω στη μέση με ένα από τα «άλλα» μαχαίρια. Έκοψα το κομμάτι του δέρματος πριονίζοντάς το, με σχετική ευκολία. Μετά μου είπε να χρησιμοποιήσω ένα από τα δικά του μαχαίρια και να κάνω το ίδιο. Το καινούργιο μαχαίρι έκοψε το δέρμα σαν να μην υπήρχε καν! Πραγματικά εντυπωσιάστηκα. Έπειτα πήρε ένα κέρμα του ενός σεντ και μου είπε να το κόψω στη μέση με το «άλλο» ψαλίδι. Προσπάθησα, αλλά απέτυχα· απλώς δεν μπορούσε να το κόψει. Μετά μου είπε να κάνω το ίδιο με το δικό του ψαλίδι. Έκοψε εύκολα το κέρμα, και πάλι εντυπωσιάστηκα με το προϊόν. Μου είπε πως τώρα ήξερα ότι αυτά τα μαχαίρια ήταν τα καλύτερα και ότι από εδώ και πέρα θα έπρεπε να μπορώ να τα πουλάω. Είχε δίκιο. Άρχισα να πουλάω μαχαίρια όπου κι αν πήγαινα! Θυμάμαι μάλιστα πως μπήκα σε ένα τροχόσπιτο που δεν το συντηρούσαν καλά, χωρίς να ελπίζω ιδιαίτερα ότι θα αγόραζαν. Προς έκπληξή μου, αγόρασαν μαχαίρια αξίας πάνω από 3.000 δολαρίων.

Ο λόγος που άρχισα να κάνω πωλήσεις είναι προφανής—πίστευα στο προϊόν μου. Παρόμοια, αν εμπιστευόμαστε τον Θεό, θα έχουμε αυτοπεποίθηση. Σε μια εποχή που οι περισσότεροι χριστιανοί που ομολογούν την πίστη τους ντρέπονται για τον Θεό και ντρέπονται να υπερασπιστούν την αλήθεια, μπορούμε να είμαστε ένα φως λαμπερό και φωτεινό. Μπορούμε να είμαστε ένας λαός που βγαίνει στον κόσμο και στις κοινότητές μας με ένα Ευαγγέλιο στο οποίο πιστεύουμε αληθινά! Όταν το κάνουμε, ο κόσμος θα το δει και θα ανταποκριθεί. Πολλοί αναζητούν· ψάχνουν απαντήσεις. Όταν κάποιος μας ρωτά γιατί κάνουμε όσα κάνουμε ή φοράμε όσα φοράμε, τι απαντάμε; Απαντάμε με σιγουριά; Έχουμε πρόχειρο κάποιο εδάφιο από τη Βίβλο; Ή ντρεπόμαστε και θα θέλαμε να ανοίξει η γη να μας καταπιεί; Αν ο κόσμος μπορούσε να δει ότι είμαστε βέβαιοι για τον Θεό μας και ότι Τον υπακούμε με ενθουσιασμό, αυτό θα ήταν μια ισχυρή μαρτυρία.

Θυμάμαι μια φορά που ταξίδευα στο αεροδρόμιο με μια μικρή ομάδα. Καθώς στεκόμασταν στην ουρά, άκουσα μια γυναίκα να ρωτά μία από τις ανύπαντρες αδελφές της ομάδας μας γιατί φορούσε αυτό το «πράγμα» στο κεφάλι της. Χάρηκα που μπορούσα να ακούω χωρίς να με προσέξουν, και ένιωσα χαρά ακούγοντας την απάντησή της. «Έχετε διαβάσει ποτέ το Α΄ Κορινθίους 11; Εκεί μας διδάσκει ότι οι γυναίκες πρέπει να καλύπτουν το κεφάλι τους. Είναι σημάδι υποταγής». Η γυναίκα ξαφνιάστηκε με την απάντησή της και είπε πως δεν είχε ξανακούσει κάτι τέτοιο και πως ο πατέρας της ήταν πάστορας. Συνέχισαν μια πολύ ενδιαφέρουσα συζήτηση, που τελείωσε με τη γυναίκα να θέλει να πάει σπίτι και να μελετήσει τη Βίβλο της.

Ένα φυλλάδιο μπορεί να κάνει πολύ καλό· το ίδιο και ένα δυνατό κήρυγμα ή ένα δημοσιευμένο άρθρο, όμως αυτό που αναζητά ο κόσμος είναι κάποιος που εμπιστεύεται τον Θεό με όλη του την καρδιά! Θέλουν να «δουν κάτι που λειτουργεί», και γιατί όχι; Ο Θεός μας θέλει να μας χρησιμοποιήσει για να δείξει τη δύναμή Του. Ασφαλώς, ο καθένας μας θέλει να τον χρησιμοποιήσει ο Θεός. Μπορούμε. Ο καθένας μας μπορεί. Η απάντηση είναι να εμπιστεύεσαι τον Κύριο με όλη σου την καρδιά και να μη στηρίζεσαι στη δική σου σύνεση –Πρ 3:5.

My Help and My Deliverer

Psalm 40:1 I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry. 2 He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings. 3 And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God: many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the LORD. 4 Blessed is that man that maketh the LORD his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies. 5 Many, O LORD my God, are thy wonderful works which thou hast done, and thy thoughts which are to us-ward: they cannot be reckoned up in order unto thee: if I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be numbered. 6 Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required. 7 Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me, 8 I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart. 9 I have preached righteousness in the great congregation: lo, I have not refrained my lips, O LORD, thou knowest. 10 I have not hid thy righteousness within my heart; I have declared thy faithfulness and thy salvation: I have not concealed thy lovingkindness and thy truth from the great congregation. 11 Withhold not thou thy tender mercies from me, O LORD: let thy lovingkindness and thy truth continually preserve me. 12 For innumerable evils have compassed me about: mine iniquities have taken hold upon me, so that I am not able to look up; they are more than the hairs of mine head: therefore my heart faileth me. 13 Be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me: O LORD, make haste to help me. 14 Let them be ashamed and confounded together that seek after my soul to destroy it; let them be driven backward and put to shame that wish me evil. 15 Let them be desolate for a reward of their shame that say unto me, Aha, aha. 16 Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: let such as love thy salvation say continually, The LORD be magnified. 17 But I am poor and needy; yet the Lord thinketh upon me: thou art my help and my deliverer; make no tarrying, O my God.

A glorious morning unfolds before me, perfect and peaceful, unmarred by failure. The sky is clear and blue. The horizon is a soft, blushing pink, enhanced by a misty fog. The distant hills and trees are shaded a dusky blue in the misty morning coolness. The morning is ringing with the warbling, twittering, chirping of birds. The grass glows with millions of dew droplets sparkling in the morning light. The pink horizon above the distant, dusky hills gradually fades into a glowing orange sphere that becomes brighter and brighter.

I stand in awe of God. My heart is thrilled at the beauty spread out before me. I am also thrilled at what God has done in my life, and the beauty He has created out of ashes.

I waited patiently for the Lord; and He inclined unto me, and heard my cry. He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings. God has brought me up out of the pit of despair and discouragement. He has set my feet upon the Rock, Jesus Christ, and He has established my goings. He knows the plans He has for me. His thoughts and His ways are much higher than mine.

He hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God: many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the Lord. I desire that God will be glorified through the work He has done and is continuing to do in my life. Many, O Lord, are Thy wonderful works which Thou hast done, and Thy thoughts which are to us-ward: they cannot be reckoned up in order unto Thee: if I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be numbered.

I delight to do Thy will, O God: yea, Thy law is within my heart. It is truly my delight to do the will of God; to love Him with my whole heart, soul, strength, and mind; to obey His commandments from my heart.

I have not hid Thy righteousness within my heart; I have declared Thy faithfulness and Thy salvation: I have not concealed Thy lovingkindness and Thy truth from the great congregation. It is such a blessing to have deep and edifying conversations with my brothers and sisters in the Lord, and to share together what the Lord is doing in our lives. It is a great strengthening to my faith.

Withhold not Thy tender mercies from me, O Lord: let Thy lovingkindness and Thy truth continually preserve me. Temptations and hard tests are a very real thing in life; the struggle to keep my heart with a diligence, the battle against stubborn pride, and the urge to utter hasty words of frustration. Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me: O Lord, make haste to help me. Let them be ashamed and confounded together that seek after my soul to destroy it; let them be driven backward and put to shame that wish me evil.

The sun has risen above the distant hills and the countryside is now glowing gloriously. The mist has faded into the woods and the distant dusky blue hills and trees have exchanged their robes for vivid shades of green intermixed with hints of red and brown. The sparkling droplets of dew are dazzling in the brilliant sunlight.

Let those that seek Thee rejoice and be glad in Thee: let such as love Thy salvation say continually, The Lord be magnified. I am poor and needy; yet the Lord thinketh upon me: Thou art my help and my deliverer; make no tarrying, O my God.

Min hjelp og min befrier

Salme 40:1 Jeg ventet tålmodig på HERREN; han bøyde seg til meg og hørte mitt rop. 2 Han drog meg opp av den fryktelige gropen, opp av den gjørmete leiren, satte mine føtter på en klippe og gjorde mine skritt faste. 3 Han la en ny sang i min munn, en lovsang til vår Gud. Mange skal se det, frykte og sette sin lit til HERREN. 4 Salig er den som setter sin lit til HERREN og ikke vender seg til de stolte eller til dem som farer med løgn. 5 Mange er dine underfulle gjerninger, HERRE, min Gud, og dine tanker for oss. Ingen kan sammenlignes med deg. Ville jeg fortelle og tale om dem, er de flere enn det kan telles. 6 Slaktoffer og grødeoffer hadde du ikke lyst til; du har åpnet mine ører. Brennoffer og syndoffer krevde du ikke. 7 Da sa jeg: «Se, jeg kommer. I bokrullen står det skrevet om meg. 8 Jeg fryder meg over å gjøre din vilje, min Gud; din lov er i mitt hjerte.» 9 Jeg har forkynt rettferdighet i den store forsamlingen. Se, jeg har ikke holdt mine lepper tilbake, HERRE, det vet du. 10 Jeg har ikke skjult din rettferdighet i mitt hjerte. Jeg har kunngjort din trofasthet og din frelse; jeg har ikke holdt din godhet og din sannhet skjult for den store forsamlingen. 11 HERRE, hold ikke din ømme barmhjertighet tilbake fra meg; la din godhet og din sannhet alltid bevare meg. 12 For utallige ulykker har omringet meg. Mine misgjerninger har innhentet meg, så jeg ikke kan løfte blikket. De er flere enn hårene på mitt hode, og mitt hjerte svikter meg. 13 Vær så snill, HERRE, å frelse meg! HERRE, skynd deg å hjelpe meg! 14 La dem som søker å ta mitt liv og ødelegge meg, bli til skamme og forvirret sammen; la dem som ønsker meg ondt, bli drevet tilbake og bli gjort til skamme. 15 La dem som sier til meg: «Aha, aha», bli øde til lønn for sin skam. 16 La alle som søker deg, fryde seg og glede seg i deg. La dem som elsker din frelse, alltid si: «HERREN være lovprist!» 17 Men jeg er fattig og trengende, og Herren tenker på meg. Du er min hjelp og min befrier. Vent ikke, min Gud.

En strålende morgen folder seg ut foran meg, fullkommen og fredfull, uten skjemmende feil. Himmelen er klar og blå. Horisonten er mykt rosa, forsterket av en tåkedis. De fjerne åsene og trærne er farget i en dunkel blå tone i den tåkete morgenkulden. Morgenluften fylles av fuglenes trillende, kvitrende og syngende toner. Gresset glitrer av millioner av duggdråper i morgenlyset. Den rosa horisonten over de fjerne, dunkle åsene går gradvis over i en glødende, oransje kule som blir stadig klarere.

Jeg står i ærefrykt for Gud. Hjertet mitt fryder seg over skjønnheten som ligger utbredt foran meg. Jeg fryder meg også over det Gud har gjort i livet mitt, og skjønnheten han har skapt av aske.

Jeg ventet tålmodig på Herren; han bøyde seg til meg og hørte mitt rop. Han drog meg opp av den fryktelige gropen, opp av den gjørmete leiren, satte mine føtter på en klippe og gjorde mine skritt faste. Gud har løftet meg opp av fortvilelsens og motløshe­tens grop. Han har satt føttene mine på Klippen, Jesus Kristus, og gjort skrittene mine faste. Han vet hvilke planer han har for meg. Hans tanker og veier er langt høyere enn mine.

Han la en ny sang i min munn, en lovsang til vår Gud. Mange skal se det, frykte og sette sin lit til Herren. Jeg ønsker at Gud skal bli herliggjort gjennom det arbeidet han har gjort og fortsatt gjør i livet mitt. Mange er dine underfulle gjerninger, Herre, som du har gjort, og dine tanker for oss. Ingen kan sammenlignes med deg. Ville jeg fortelle og tale om dem, er de flere enn det kan telles.

Jeg fryder meg over å gjøre din vilje, Gud; din lov er i mitt hjerte. Det er virkelig min glede å gjøre Guds vilje; å elske ham av hele mitt hjerte, min sjel, min styrke og min forstand; å adlyde hans bud av hjertet.

Jeg har ikke skjult din rettferdighet i mitt hjerte. Jeg har kunngjort din trofasthet og din frelse; jeg har ikke holdt din godhet og din sannhet skjult for den store forsamlingen. Det er en slik velsignelse å ha dype og oppbyggende samtaler med mine brødre og søstre i Herren og dele med hverandre det Herren gjør i livene våre. Det styrker troen min veldig.

HERRE, hold ikke din ømme barmhjertighet tilbake fra meg; la din godhet og din sannhet alltid bevare meg. Fristelser og harde prøvelser er en svært reell del av livet; kampen for å vokte hjertet mitt med all flid, kampen mot sta stolthet og trangen til å komme med forhastede ord av frustrasjon. Today, I’d like to continue and possibly complete our discussion of Regenerative Medicine. I want to consider where it stands today, and how Christians can navigate the complex maze of treatments. As you may recall, in the previous issue of this magazine we discussed that Regenerative Medicine is man’s attempt to re-create organ systems. We described how fetal tissue was attempted to be used, due to its low rate of rejection by the people receiving it. Medically speaking, it was problematic in that, if used on a large scale, it would require large amounts of aborted fetuses. Later, embryonic stem cells were studied in depth. Here, embryos, which are newly conceived humans in their earliest stages, are dissected (cut apart) and stem cells are taken.

Think of stem cells as indolent, immature adults, who live in their parents’ basements, without direction, not knowing what they want to do with their lives. With a little encouragement and direction, they can finally find their way, finding a specialized skill and important role in life. In like manner, scientists have discovered ways to “program” these stem cells, “encouraging” them to become specialized into types of cells, such as nerve, heart, blood, and insulin producing. These cells would then be grown in a lab, then used to repair or replace the diseased or injured tissue.

However, “taking” stem cells from embryos results in his or her (the embryo’s) destruction. This is obviously problematic for Christians, knowing that one of the seven things that the Lord says is an abomination is …hands that shed innocent blood –Pro 6:17. Additionally, the sixth commandment directs, Thou shalt not kill –Exo 20:13. Because these objections were recognized by the scientific community, there was pressure to find an alternative.

The Apostle Paul states, There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it –1Co 10:13. His words are as true today as they were 2000 years ago. While Christians suffer from disease just as commonly as non-Christians do, modern medicine can present the “temptation” of a treatment and relief from disease or injury that is actually immoral. But God is faithful, and his escape is twofold. First and foremost, He gave His son to bear our burdens. It is to this Great Physician that we should always turn to first.

In the case of stem cell treatments, it so happens that it was discovered that these immature stem cells are not only found in human embryos, but they are also found in all people, from infants to grown-ups as well. This may be the physical “escape” for His faithful children. These immature stem cells (usually obtained from a patient’s fat tissue or bone marrow) can be grown, cultured, and used just as well as embryonic stem cells. It turns out that “Adult Stem Cells” have actually been more clinically effective, since they are “custom designed” for each individual, and since they come from that person’s own body; therefore, there is very little problem with rejection.

Umbilical cord stem cells have also been shown to be useful, particularly in bone and cartilage treatments. Just as there have been obstacles to overcome when using embryonic stem cells, so too there are problems with developing treatments using adult or umbilical cord stem cells. Think again of a stem cell as an immature, indolent adult. Just having him “hang out” with a master carpenter will not make him a master carpenter if all he does is find entertainment on his cell phone. Stem cells, like an apprentice, need intense, focused training and direction to become specialists in their chosen field of expertise. Learning how to turn these “switches” on is perhaps one of the greatest challenges. The main idea here is that just injecting stem cells that have not been “programmed” or “trained” into damaged or diseased tissue will not automatically make them “know” what to become or how to function.

Similarly, just putting a young electronics apprentice on a bus that is traveling into a city that just had a power grid failure will not result in restoring the power. Here the parallel is placing stem cells into the brain of a stroke victim or a paraplegic accident victim, hoping that the stem cells will “know” what to do, and which specific connections to repair in order to restore function. This may not work as hoped. It would be fruitless to expect success unless and until these problems are also addressed.

Then there is the lingering problem of these eager youngsters (stem cells) knowing when to stop. The problem with fetal tissue turning into cancerous tumors is also a problem to be dealt with in stem cells. Considering this, there is one exception: umbilical cord stem cells are generally not known to turn malignant.1

Here is a short list of treatments that are in development that would use stem cells:

  • Macular Degeneration—Repair a damaged retina.
  • Spinal Cord Injury/Stroke—Repair nerve tissue.
  • Burns—Repair skin tissue.
  • Congestive Heart Failure—Repair damaged heart tissue.
  • Diabetes—Replace or increase the pancreatic tissue that makes insulin.
  • Arthritis—Repair damaged cartilage.
  • Autoimmune diseases (Lupus, Multiple Sclerosis) —Destroy the immune system that is attacking its own body and replace or “reset” it with a new immune system derived from one’s own stem cells.
  • Leukemias—Destroy the cancerous blood cells and replace them with new stem cell derived blood cells.
  • New organs—Replace diseased, damaged, or cancer-ridden organs, such as the kidney, liver, or pancreas, with organs derived from the patient’s own stem cells, grown in a lab, and transplanted surgically, without the need of anti-rejection drugs.

As you can see, there is a very long list of diseases and ailments that may result in effective treatments with stem cells. I am very optimistic that within a decade, remedies for many of these ailments will be commonly available. However, learning how to make stem cells that are expertly specialized into specific tissue types, learning how to turn stems cells on and then turning them off at the necessary time (once the job is finished), and learning how to “teach” the stem cells where and how to make repairs will take time.

I am not the only one who is excited about the possibilities. That is why hundreds of stem cell clinics have sprung up across the country, trying to get in on the excitement. But do the claims of any of these clinics align with reality? Which ones are legitimate? I know that there are many clinics offering stem cell treatments for various ailments, so let’s now look at some of the treatments that are available today—ones that have evidence of actually helping, as well as realistic expectations. Let’s also look at some of the possible complications, to help us make informed decisions.

First, the risks and complications

  • Introduction of infection—For example, bacteria living on the skin can enter a joint space from a simple injection, resulting in destruction of the joint, even under the cleanest of conditions.
  • Stems cells moving from their introduction site and not going where they are intended or not staying contained to the specific area of treatment—One study involving pigs treated with stem cells injected into areas of a damaged heart after a heart attack showed near complete return of function, but then the new heart tissue kept growing, eventually filling the heart’s pumping chamber, which caused all the pigs to die.
  • Stem cells changing into unexpected or inappropriate cell types—Stem cells used for a facial cosmetic effect have actually turned to bone.2
  • Growth of tumors—There are documented cases of different tumors, including brain and kidney tumors that have developed after patients were treated for stroke and kidney failure using stem cells.
  • Failure to work as expected—There are documented cases of people with macular degeneration, who were treated with stem cells injected into the eye, that have resulted in blindness.
  • Stem cells can’t be withdrawn—Unlike medicines such as a pill or an injection, if something goes wrong, one can’t just withhold the next dose. Once stem cells are introduced, they can’t be taken back. The course that has been set will continue.

The rates of complications are hard to know, since there are no reporting requirements when performed outside of formal clinical investigations.

Next, the known benefits

The FDA (the governmental Food and Drug Administration that is tasked with health safety) has approved stem cell treatments for dozens of blood cancers (leukemias) and blood diseases using umbilical cord stem cells. Though not FDA approved, studies have shown some benefit for using stem cells for orthopedic applications, particularly arthritis of the knees. (Using stem cells for such orthopedic uses, without the need to stimulate them to become cartilage cells beforehand, appears to be the exception to the rule. Remember most stem cells need to be specialized before being used.) That’s it! Aside from this, most other uses for stem cells should only be considered either highly experimental or highly suspect of exaggerated benefits. Could there be other beneficial treatments that are not FDA approved? Perhaps, but it’s important to realize that the claims have often far outpaced the science.

So how is one to know? Here are some things to consider when choosing providers of stem cell treatments, as well as red flags, to tell you if there are better places to go for your health care. (These points are also true for just about any other treatment):

  1. Informed consent—Every medical treatment has risks and benefits. These should be routinely discussed with you beforehand, without you needing to ask. Any practitioner who claims there are no risks, only benefits, either is not sufficiently knowledgeable or is not sufficiently honest!
  2. Can they handle the complications? —Joint injections can sometimes result in infection. These can be severe infections that can potentially destroy the joint. Such complications are not just simply treated with antibiotics, but with surgery. These stem cell treatments are better handled by an orthopedic surgeon or practitioner that has a close relationship with one, if complications should arise. Likewise, treatments involving nerves should be done by neurologists or neurosurgeons.
  3. Is the clinic adequately equipped? —Stem cells need to be handled appropriately. The transport of umbilical stem cells and improper thawing from the supplier can drastically reduce numbers, which may have a great deal to do with determining the success of the procedure. Additionally, these cells may be in a state of “shock,” unless they are appropriately re-cultured after being thawed. This allows them to re-enter a desirable growth phase again.3 This may mean having a specialized lab and microbiologist on staff to properly grow and care for the stem cells, ensuring good quality control. This usually requires a university setting, not just a small clinic or office that has a nurse to thaw the stem cells after receiving them from an overnight delivery service. Glitzy web sites, colorful brochures, and informational dinners are not enough.
  4. Guinea pigs and rats are “experimented on,” people go through “clinical trials.” —Please avoid any practitioner who says they are doing experiments. Clinical trials involving people, which have the oversight of ethics boards, only occur after experiments on animals have shown low risk of harm, and a good chance of success. If a treatment is very effective, the FDA has suggested that as few as 42 participants can demonstrate adequate safety to grant approval. This is not an outrageously high threshold to overcome. Additionally, patients involved in clinical trials are usually only expected to cover minimal costs, if any. Practitioners who “experiment” on people rarely do it for free.4
  5. Realistic claims. —Does your practitioner claim 100 percent success? If so, it is better to run away (if your knees will allow you to) than to simply walk away! Knee treatments, for example, may only delay knee replacements for many people. Some may avoid surgery, but certainly not all. Do not expect a cure. Also, do they make claims well outside of what is commonly recognized? “Cures” claimed for Alzheimers, Parkinson’s, or other ailments that are not FDA approved? I cannot totally exclude the possibility that such treatments may exist at some future time. However, these practitioners should be able to point to (and provide to you) published studies. If there is a miraculous cure, the world should be able to benefit from it, and he or she should be able to patent it, so as to reap the financial benefits of sharing their techniques and discoveries with the rest of the world. By doing so, it is independently tested and verified. Anyone who has a “secret” cure, that they alone possess, should be avoided.
  1. Does it make sense? —By simply injecting stem cells (that have not been induced by a lab into their specialty state such as nerve cells, heart cells, etc.) into the bloodstream to treat things like nerve disorders, for example, does not make sense. Clinical trials of legitimate treatments first specialize the stem cells, then directly apply them to the affected area. For example, specific types of nerve cells are injected directly into specific locations of the brain, and heart cells are injected directly into the scarred tissue of the heart. Remember the indolent adult (the unspecialized stem cell)? You can’t expect to put them on a bus (inject them into a vein), send them into the big city (the body), without instructions on what to do (leaving them unspecialized), not knowing where to go (to somehow find the diseased part of the body) and then magically expect success.
  2. The hard sell. —Are you being told that or are you made to feel that you are “missing out” if you decline? Do the clinic advertisements have testimonial bylines, something to the effect of “Individual results may vary, and testimonials are not claimed to represent typical results and are not intended to represent or guarantee that anyone will achieve the same or similar results…”? As the old adage goes, if it’s too good to be true (especially if they actually tell you so), then it probably is. In these cases, consider the claims to be most likely somewhat exaggerated, and also consider working with someone who can give a more honest set of expectations.

I pray that God may grant you wisdom: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him –Jas 1:5.

I dag vil jeg gjerne fortsette og kanskje avslutte diskusjonen vår om regenerativ medisin. Jeg vil se på hvor den står i dag, og hvordan kristne kan finne veien gjennom den kompliserte labyrinten av behandlinger. Som dere kanskje husker, diskuterte vi i forrige nummer av dette magasinet at regenerativ medisin er menneskets forsøk på å gjenskape organsystemer. Vi beskrev hvordan man forsøkte å bruke fostervev, fordi det hadde lav avstøtningsrate hos dem som mottok det. Medisinsk sett var dette problematisk fordi bruk i stor skala ville kreve store mengder aborterte fostre. Senere ble embryonale stamceller studert inngående. Her blir embryoer, som er mennesker som nylig er unnfanget og befinner seg på sine aller tidligste utviklingsstadier, dissekert (skåret opp), og stamceller tas ut.

Tenk på stamceller som late, umodne voksne som bor i foreldrenes kjeller, uten retning og uten å vite hva de vil gjøre med livet sitt. Med litt oppmuntring og veiledning kan de endelig finne veien, finne en spesialisert ferdighet og en viktig rolle i livet. På samme måte har forskere oppdaget måter å «programmere» disse stamcellene på, «oppmuntre» dem til å utvikle seg til spesialiserte celletyper, som nerve-, hjerte- og blodceller, samt insulinproduserende celler. Disse cellene kan deretter dyrkes i et laboratorium og brukes til å reparere eller erstatte sykt eller skadet vev.

Men å «ta» stamceller fra embryoer fører til at embryoet blir ødelagt. Dette er åpenbart problematisk for kristne, som vet at én av de sju tingene Herren sier er en styggedom, er …hender som utøser uskyldig blod –Ordsp 6,17. I tillegg sier det sjette budet: Du skal ikke slå ihjel –2 Mos 20,13. Fordi det vitenskapelige miljøet innså disse innvendingene, oppsto det et press for å finne et alternativ.

Apostelen Paulus sier: Dere har ikke møtt noen fristelse som mennesker ikke kan tåle. Gud er trofast, han vil ikke la dere bli fristet over evne, men gjøre både fristelsen og utgangen fra den slik at dere kan holde ut –1 Kor 10,13. Hans ord er like sanne i dag som de var for 2000 år siden. Kristne rammes av sykdom like ofte som ikke-kristne, men moderne medisin kan by på en «fristelse» i form av en behandling og lindring av sykdom eller skade som faktisk er umoralsk. Men Gud er trofast, og hans utvei er todelt. Først og fremst ga han sin Sønn for at han skulle bære byrdene våre. Det er til denne store legen vi alltid først bør vende oss.

Når det gjelder stamcellebehandlinger, viste det seg at disse umodne stamcellene ikke bare finnes i menneskelige embryoer, men også hos alle mennesker, fra spedbarn til voksne. Dette kan være den fysiske «utveien» for hans trofaste barn. Disse umodne stamcellene (som vanligvis hentes fra pasientens fettvev eller benmarg) kan dyrkes, formeres og brukes like godt som embryonale stamceller. Det viser seg at «voksne stamceller» faktisk har vært mer effektive klinisk, siden de er «skreddersydd» for hver enkelt og kommer fra personens egen kropp; derfor er det svært liten fare for avstøtning.

Stamceller fra navlestreng har også vist seg nyttige, særlig ved behandling av bein og brusk. Akkurat som det har vært hindringer å overvinne ved bruk av embryonale stamceller, er det også problemer med å utvikle behandlinger ved hjelp av stamceller fra voksne eller navlestreng. Tenk igjen på en stamcelle som en umoden, lat voksen. Det at han bare «henger sammen med» en mestersnekker, gjør ham ikke til en mestersnekker hvis alt han gjør, er å finne underholdning på mobiltelefonen sin. Stamceller trenger, som lærlinger, intensiv og målrettet opplæring og veiledning for å bli spesialister innen sitt valgte fagfelt. Å lære hvordan man slår på disse «bryterne», er kanskje en av de største utfordringene. Hovedpoenget her er at det å injisere stamceller som ikke er «programmert» eller «trent» i skadet eller sykt vev, ikke automatisk får dem til å «vite» hva de skal bli eller hvordan de skal fungere.

På samme måte vil det ikke føre til at strømmen kommer tilbake bare å plassere en ung elektronikerlærling på en buss som kjører inn i en by der strømnettet nettopp har sviktet. Parallellen her er å plassere stamceller i hjernen til et slagoffer eller en person som er blitt lam etter en ulykke, i håp om at stamcellene skal «vite» hva de skal gjøre, og hvilke bestemte forbindelser de skal reparere for å gjenopprette funksjonen. Dette fungerer kanskje ikke slik man håper. Det ville være nytteløst å forvente at det skal lykkes før og med mindre også disse problemene blir løst.

Så er det det vedvarende problemet med at disse ivrige ungdommene (stamcellene) må vite når de skal stoppe. Problemet med at fostervev utvikler seg til kreftsvulster, er også et problem som må håndteres når det gjelder stamceller. Når dette tas i betraktning, finnes det ett unntak: Stamceller fra navlestreng er vanligvis ikke kjent for å bli ondartede.1

Her er en kort liste over behandlinger under utvikling som vil bruke stamceller:

  • Makuladegenerasjon – reparere en skadet netthinne.
  • Ryggmargsskade/hjerneslag – reparere nervevev.
  • Brannskader – reparere hudvev.
  • Kongestiv hjertesvikt – reparere skadet hjertevev.
  • Diabetes – erstatte eller øke mengden bukspyttkjertelvev som produserer insulin.
  • Artritt – reparere skadet brusk.
  • Autoimmune sykdommer (lupus, multippel sklerose) – ødelegge immunforsvaret som angriper kroppen selv, og erstatte det eller «nullstille» det med et nytt immunforsvar som er utviklet fra ens egne stamceller.
  • Leukemier – ødelegge de kreftsyke blodcellene og erstatte dem med nye blodceller utviklet fra stamceller.
  • Nye organer – erstatte syke, skadede eller kreftbefengte organer, som nyre, lever eller bukspyttkjertel, med organer som er utviklet fra pasientens egne stamceller, dyrket i et laboratorium og transplantert kirurgisk, uten behov for avstøtningshemmende legemidler.

Som dere ser, er listen over sykdommer og plager som kan føre til effektive stamcellebehandlinger, svært lang. Jeg er svært optimistisk med tanke på at behandlinger for mange av disse plagene vil bli allment tilgjengelige i løpet av et tiår. Men det vil ta tid å lære hvordan man lager stamceller som er spesialisert på bestemte vevstyper, hvordan man slår stamcellene på og deretter av på riktig tidspunkt (når jobben er gjort), og hvordan man «lærer» stamcellene hvor og hvordan de skal reparere.

Jeg er ikke den eneste som er begeistret for mulighetene. Derfor har hundrevis av stamcelleklinikker dukket opp over hele landet i et forsøk på å få en del av begeistringen. Men stemmer påstandene fra noen av disse klinikkene med virkeligheten? Hvilke av dem er seriøse? Jeg vet at mange klinikker tilbyr stamcellebehandlinger for ulike plager, så la oss nå se på noen av behandlingene som er tilgjengelige i dag – behandlinger det finnes dokumentasjon for at faktisk hjelper, og som bygger på realistiske forventninger. La oss også se på noen av de mulige komplikasjonene, slik at vi kan ta velinformerte beslutninger.

Først: risikoer og komplikasjoner

  • Infeksjon – Bakterier som lever på huden, kan for eksempel komme inn i et ledd gjennom en enkel injeksjon og føre til at leddet ødelegges, selv under de reneste forhold.
  • Stamceller som beveger seg bort fra stedet der de ble satt inn, ikke kommer dit de er ment å komme, eller ikke forblir avgrenset til det bestemte behandlingsområdet – En studie der griser fikk stamceller injisert i områder av et skadet hjerte etter et hjerteinfarkt, viste at funksjonen nesten ble fullstendig gjenopprettet. Men det nye hjertevevet fortsatte å vokse og fylte til slutt hjertets pumpekammer, noe som førte til at alle grisene døde.
  • Stamceller som utvikler seg til uventede eller uegnede celletyper – Stamceller som ble brukt for å oppnå en kosmetisk effekt i ansiktet, utviklet seg faktisk til beinvev.2
  • Svulstvekst – Det finnes dokumenterte tilfeller av ulike svulster, blant annet i hjernen og nyrene, som har utviklet seg etter at pasienter ble behandlet med stamceller for hjerneslag og nyresvikt.
  • Behandlingen virker ikke som forventet – Det finnes dokumenterte tilfeller der personer med makuladegenerasjon som ble behandlet med stamceller injisert i øyet, er blitt blinde.
  • Stamceller kan ikke trekkes tilbake – I motsetning til legemidler som en pille eller en injeksjon kan man ikke bare la være å gi neste dose hvis noe går galt. Når stamcellene først er satt inn, kan de ikke tas tilbake. Forløpet som er satt i gang, vil fortsette.

Det er vanskelig å vite hvor ofte komplikasjoner oppstår, siden det ikke stilles krav om rapportering når behandlingene utføres utenfor formelle kliniske studier.

Deretter: kjente fordeler

FDA (det statlige organet Food and Drug Administration, som har ansvar for helsesikkerhet) har godkjent stamcellebehandlinger for en rekke blodkreftsykdommer (leukemier) og blodsykdommer ved bruk av stamceller fra navlestreng. Selv om de ikke er godkjent av FDA, har studier vist at stamceller kan ha en viss nytte ved ortopediske tilstander, særlig kneartrose. (Bruk av stamceller til slike ortopediske formål, uten at de først må stimuleres til å bli bruskceller, ser ut til å være et unntak fra regelen. Husk at de fleste stamceller må spesialiseres før de brukes.) Det er alt! Bortsett fra dette bør de fleste andre bruksområder for stamceller bare betraktes som svært eksperimentelle eller som svært mistenkelige med tanke på overdrevne fordeler. Kan det finnes andre nyttige behandlinger som ikke er godkjent av FDA? Kanskje, men det er viktig å innse at påstandene ofte har ligget langt foran vitenskapen.

Hvordan skal man da vite? Her er noen ting å tenke på når man velger tilbydere av stamcellebehandling, og noen varselsignaler som kan fortelle deg om det finnes bedre steder å få helsehjelp. (Disse punktene gjelder også for nesten alle andre behandlinger):

  1. Informert samtykke – Alle medisinske behandlinger har risikoer og fordeler. Disse bør rutinemessig diskuteres med deg på forhånd, uten at du trenger å spørre. Enhver behandler som hevder at det ikke finnes risikoer, bare fordeler, er enten ikke tilstrekkelig kunnskapsrik eller ikke tilstrekkelig ærlig!
  2. Kan de håndtere komplikasjonene? – Leddinjeksjoner kan noen ganger føre til infeksjon. Dette kan være alvorlige infeksjoner som potensielt kan ødelegge leddet. Slike komplikasjoner behandles ikke bare med antibiotika, men med kirurgi. Disse stamcellebehandlingene håndteres best av en ortopedisk kirurg eller en behandler som har et nært samarbeid med en slik kirurg, dersom det skulle oppstå komplikasjoner. Tilsvarende bør behandlinger som involverer nerver, utføres av nevrologer eller nevrokirurger.
  3. Er klinikken tilstrekkelig utstyrt? – Stamceller må håndteres på riktig måte. Transport av stamceller fra navlestreng og feilaktig tining hos leverandøren kan redusere antallet drastisk, noe som kan ha mye å si for hvor vellykket behandlingen blir. I tillegg kan disse cellene være i en tilstand av «sjokk» hvis de ikke dyrkes på nytt på riktig måte etter tining. Dette gjør at de igjen kan gå inn i en ønskelig vekstfase.3 Det kan bety at klinikken må ha et spesialisert laboratorium og en mikrobiolog ansatt som kan dyrke og ta godt vare på stamcellene og sikre god kvalitetskontroll. Dette krever vanligvis et universitetsmiljø, ikke bare en liten klinikk eller et legekontor der en sykepleier tiner stamcellene etter at de er mottatt med en ekspresstjeneste over natten. Prangende nettsteder, fargerike brosjyrer og informasjonsmiddager er ikke nok.
  4. Det er marsvin og rotter man «eksperimenterer på»; mennesker deltar i «kliniske studier». – Unngå behandlere som sier at de eksperimenterer. Kliniske studier med mennesker, som følges opp av etiske komiteer, finner bare sted etter at dyreforsøk har vist lav risiko for skade og god sannsynlighet for å lykkes. Hvis en behandling er svært effektiv, har FDA antydet at så få som 42 deltakere kan vise tilstrekkelig sikkerhet til at godkjenning kan gis. Dette er ikke en urimelig høy terskel å komme over. Pasienter som deltar i kliniske studier, forventes dessuten vanligvis bare å dekke minimale kostnader, om noen. Behandlere som «eksperimenterer» på mennesker, gjør det sjelden gratis.4
  5. Realistiske påstander. – Hevder behandleren din at behandlingen har 100 prosent suksessrate? I så fall er det bedre å løpe sin vei (hvis knærne dine tillater det) enn bare å gå sin vei! Knebehandlinger kan for eksempel bare utsette behovet for kneprotese for mange mennesker. Noen kan unngå kirurgi, men slett ikke alle. Ikke forvent en kur. Kommer de også med påstander som ligger langt utenfor det som er allment anerkjent? «Kurer» for Alzheimers, Parkinsons eller andre plager som ikke er godkjent av FDA? Jeg kan ikke helt utelukke muligheten for at slike behandlinger kan finnes en gang i framtiden. Disse behandlerne bør imidlertid kunne vise til (og gi deg) publiserte studier. Hvis det finnes en mirakuløs kur, bør resten av verden kunne dra nytte av den, og behandleren bør kunne ta patent på den for å høste de økonomiske fordelene ved å dele teknikkene og oppdagelsene sine med resten av verden. På denne måten blir den testet og verifisert uavhengig. Man bør unngå alle som har en «hemmelig» kur som bare de selv kjenner til.
  1. Gir det mening? – Det gir for eksempel ikke mening å behandle nervesykdommer ved ganske enkelt å injisere stamceller i blodbanen, når de ikke er blitt stimulert i et laboratorium til å utvikle seg til sin spesialiserte form, som nerveceller, hjerteceller og så videre. I kliniske studier av legitime behandlinger spesialiserer man først stamcellene og tilfører dem deretter direkte til det berørte området. For eksempel injiseres bestemte typer nerveceller direkte på bestemte steder i hjernen, og hjerteceller injiseres direkte i arrvevet i hjertet. Husk den late voksne (den uspesialiserte stamcellen). Du kan ikke forvente at du kan sette dem på en buss (injisere dem i en blodåre), sende dem inn i storbyen (kroppen) uten instruksjoner om hva de skal gjøre (la dem være uspesialiserte), uten at de vet hvor de skal (for på et vis å finne den syke delen av kroppen), og så på magisk vis forvente at det skal lykkes.
  2. Det aggressive salget. – Blir du fortalt, eller får du følelsen av, at du «går glipp av noe» hvis du takker nei? Har klinikkens annonser vitnesbyrd med en merknad av typen «Resultatene kan variere fra person til person, og vitnesbyrdene hevdes ikke å representere typiske resultater og er ikke ment å representere eller garantere at noen vil oppnå samme eller lignende resultater …»? Som det gamle ordtaket sier: Hvis noe virker for godt til å være sant (særlig hvis de faktisk forteller deg det), er det sannsynligvis det. I slike tilfeller bør du regne med at påstandene mest sannsynlig er noe overdrevne, og også vurdere å samarbeide med noen som kan gi deg mer ærlige forventninger.

Jeg ber om at Gud må gi dere visdom: Om noen av dere mangler visdom, skal han be til Gud, han som gir alle villig og uten bebreidelse, og så skal han få –Jak 1,5.

Særskilt merknad:

Noen foreldre har gitt uttrykk for interesse for å ta med barna sine til Japan for å vaksinere dem der, hvis vi ikke kan få vaksinene sendt til USA. Hvis det er andre lesere av dette magasinet som også er interessert, ber jeg dere ta kontakt med The Berean Voice, slik at vi kan planlegge og koordinere dette. If marriage is a covenant, what is the significance of covenant relationship? What makes it a covenant relationship, and how does this differ from any other relationship? These are answers that we must pursue if we are to understand the permanence of marriage and if we are to successfully navigate the rocky shores of a troubled marriage.

Covenant in our society has become archaic. The cultural revolution of the sixties has made divorce culturally acceptable, and life-long fidelity in marriage has become the exception rather than the rule. Unfortunately, this blight has infected most mainstream churches and is currently invading our Anabaptist churches.

Covenant is God’s idea. He is the primary covenant maker. His holy name “Jehovah” indicates that God is always true to His word. The Hebrew origin of “Jehovah” is yeh-ho-vaw. This word combines two Hebrew verbs of being. A most literal translation for the name yeh-ho-vaw would be (is is) or as God said to Moses “I am that I am.”

God’s name “Jehovah” indicates that God is always true to His word, that he cannot lie, and that He is true to His character. James states it this way: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning –Jas 1:17.

What makes a covenant?

Careful investigation of scripture will reveal that there are three key elements in the establishment of a covenant.

  • Words
  • Witnesses
  • That which ratifies the covenant

Words

Words define the terms and conditions of a covenant. It is very important that the terms and conditions of the covenant be clearly defined and understood by both parties involved. When God made covenant with Abraham, He spake and said, And I will establish my covenant between me and thee and thy seed after thee in their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God unto thee, and to thy seed after thee –Gen 17:7.

When God made covenant with the nation of Israel at Mt Sinai, He gave them the Law which was the terms and conditions of the Mosaic covenant.

In our Bibles today we have the Old and the New Testament. This refers to the Old and the New Covenant. In the New Testament we have the teachings of Jesus and His Apostles which supersede the Old Testament law. In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus said repeatedly, “You have heard that it hath been said, but I say unto you.”

The Hebrew writer had this to say about the New Covenant: But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises –Heb 8:6.

On our wedding day we use words with precise meaning to establish a covenant that is binding “…till death do us part.” Wedding vows may contain some variation but should always include a commitment to a mutually loving relationship that is binding for life, and thus irrevocable.

Witnesses

Another important part of a covenant is the witnesses. Witnesses provide validation and accountability to the vows that have been made. This is especially true of a covenant made between two people.

When Joshua re-established the covenant with Israel upon entering the land of Canaan, he challenged them: And Joshua said unto the people, Ye are witnesses against yourselves that ye have chosen you the LORD, to serve him. And they said, We are witnesses –Jos 24:22. What they were saying was that, “We will hold one another accountable for the commitments that we are making today.”

Regarding the New Covenant, we have the testimony of the Apostle John where he says: For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one. And there are three that bear witness in earth, the Spirit, and the water, and the blood: and these three agree in one –1Joh 5:7-8. Here John is saying that in this New Covenant between God and man there are three witnesses in heaven and three witnesses in earth, and these witnesses all agree.

In the establishment of a marriage covenant the wedding guests are the witnesses. Every guest becomes a witness of the vows that are made. By their presence and blessing, they validate the marriage and become personally responsible to ensure that this marriage endures.

This community commitment to the permanence of marriage is the moral fabric of our society and our churches. When a society becomes negligent in enforcing the permanence of marriage, chaos and confusion ensue. We see this in the society around us. Unfortunately, we are also seeing an increasing number of marriage breakups within our Anabaptist churches.

That which ratifies the covenant

The final step in establishing a covenant is that which ratifies and renders binding and effective the terms of the covenant. Historically there have been a variety of methods of binding a covenant. Ancient Bedouins had a practice of using salt to bind a covenant. Each party would give to the other a measure of salt. The salt was mixed with their respective stores of salt making it impossible to ever separate “my salt” from “your salt.” This symbolized the immutability of this treaty.

Then there was the practice of berith. Berith is a Hebrew word that means “to cut.” In ancient Israel a covenant was ratified by “cutting a covenant.” This practice is clearly illustrated in Genesis 15 where God ratified His covenant with Abraham. Abraham asked God, …Lord GOD, whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it? –Gen 15:8. God’s response to Abraham’s plea was …Take me an heifer of three years old, and a she goat of three years old, and a ram of three years old, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon –Gen 15:9. Abraham took these animals and divided them in the midst and lay them out as a sacrifice to God. God reaffirmed His covenant with Abraham (with words), and then in verse 17, we have this mysterious event: And it came to pass, that, when the sun went down, and it was dark, behold a smoking furnace, and a burning lamp that passed between those pieces –Gen 15:17. This was “berith” or the “cutting of the covenant.” This ceremony ratified and rendered binding the terms and conditions of the covenant. After this event, we have no record that Abraham ever questioned or doubted the promise of God, although he did take it into his own hands to bring that promise to fruition.

When God made covenant with Israel at Mt Sinai, …Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which the LORD hath made with you concerning all these words –Exo 24:8. This blood rendered binding and effective the terms and conditions set forth in the law—this was the Old Covenant.

When God made covenant with you and I at Mt Calvary, the blood of Jesus became the ratifying evidence or the binding token of His New Covenant with us. When we partake of the communion, we are commemorating the covenant that we have with God through Christ.

What ratifies the marriage covenant? As we have already seen, in a marriage we have words (the vows), and we have witnesses (the guests). Does this complete the marriage? No. The marriage is not complete until there is a coming together in physical intimacy. This completes or, as we sometimes say, consummates the marriage covenant. This is that which ratifies and renders binding and permanent the terms and conditions of the marriage covenant. Early on in Scripture we have example of this. And Adam knew Eve his wife… Gen 4:1. Then later on we see another example, And Isaac brought her [Rebekah] into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her… –Gen 24:67. Physical oneness belongs to covenant. This is why such a relationship outside of marriage is sin. Fornication or adultery takes that which God has ordained to be inextricably linked to marriage and adulterates the covenant.

When a married couple comes together in physical union they are commemorating and celebrating their marriage covenant. This is the start of them establishing a biblical “one flesh” reality. From this blessed union new life emerges in the form of precious “little ones” and of hearts that are renewed by the power of love.

When we partake of the bread and the wine of communion we are commemorating and celebrating our covenant relationship with Christ. From this blessed oneness new life emerges in the form of hearts that are renewed by the power of love. This is the strength of covenant.

Where these three elements exist—vows, witnesses, and that which ratifies—we have a covenant relationship. How does a covenant relationship differ from any other relationship?

A commitment to fidelity

Some of the most noble words that human lips can utter are “I promise to love you till death do us part.” On our wedding day these words are easy to utter, and we may be most sincere when we speak them. The fact is that no one can possibly know what those words may cost in the course of a lifetime.

Love is a choice and must become established and endure as an every day walk of life. We must choose to direct our affection toward the one of our covenant love and away from the enticements of others. Many, many marriages are destroyed through infidelity.

God has designed marriage to be powerfully bonding. The spiritual, emotional, and physical attachment of marriage creates an inseparable bond. In Genesis we read Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh –Gen 2:24. The word cleave in this verse denotes “being welded or glued together in such a way as to be inseparable.”

To break the marriage bond through infidelity causes rending and wounding to both parties. Satan, the great deceiver, would have us to believe that being unfaithful to our spouse will somehow benefit us. This is a huge lie.

A commitment to faithfulness

God demonstrated covenant faithfulness in his dealings with His Old Testament bride—the nation of Israel. She was not true to her covenant vows. She turned from the worship of Jehovah, and she bowed her knee to pagan altars. Despite her unfaithfulness, God continued to pursue her and call her back unto himself. Israel’s unfaithfulness did not alter God’s faithfulness. This is the strength of covenant love. Covenant love is not contingent upon the actions of the other party. Covenant love persists even though it is not reciprocated. This is a kingdom concept. Paul taught, Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head –Rom 12:20. Would this principle not most aptly apply to a broken marriage?

The strength of covenant can only be fully realized through an understanding of the divine love of God for us. Our salvation is dependent upon God’s perfect love for us. He continues to love us even though our love for Him is sometimes flawed. His unfailing love continues to draw us back unto himself. The strength of covenant in marriage is found in seeking to emulate this divine love. This divine love will not be found in romance novels or other books on marriage. This divine love can only be found in an intimate relationship with “The Source” of undying love.

Se o casamento é uma aliança, qual é o significado de um relacionamento de aliança? O que faz dele um relacionamento de aliança, e em que difere de qualquer outro relacionamento? Essas são respostas que precisamos buscar se quisermos compreender a permanência do casamento e navegar com sucesso pelas águas turbulentas de um casamento em crise.

Em nossa sociedade, a aliança tornou-se algo arcaico. A revolução cultural dos anos sessenta tornou o divórcio culturalmente aceitável, e a fidelidade conjugal por toda a vida passou a ser a exceção, em vez da regra. Infelizmente, essa praga contaminou a maioria das igrejas tradicionais e atualmente está invadindo nossas igrejas anabatistas.

A aliança é uma ideia de Deus. Ele é o principal autor de alianças. Seu santo nome, “Jeová”, indica que Deus é sempre fiel à sua palavra. A origem hebraica de “Jeová” é yeh-ho-vaw. Essa palavra combina dois verbos hebraicos de existência. A tradução mais literal do nome yeh-ho-vaw seria “é é”, ou, como Deus disse a Moisés: “Eu sou o que sou”.

O nome de Deus, “Jeová”, indica que Deus é sempre fiel à sua palavra, que não pode mentir e que é fiel ao seu caráter. Tiago expressa isso desta maneira: Toda boa dádiva e todo dom perfeito vêm do alto, descendo do Pai das luzes, em quem não há mudança nem sombra de variação – Tg 1:17.

O que constitui uma aliança?

Um exame cuidadoso das Escrituras revelará que há três elementos essenciais para estabelecer uma aliança.

  • Palavras
  • Testemunhas
  • Aquilo que ratifica a aliança

Palavras

As palavras definem os termos e as condições de uma aliança. É muito importante que os termos e as condições da aliança sejam claramente definidos e compreendidos por ambas as partes envolvidas. Quando Deus fez uma aliança com Abraão, falou e disse: E estabelecerei a minha aliança entre mim e ti e a tua descendência depois de ti, nas suas gerações, por aliança perpétua, para ser o teu Deus e o da tua descendência depois de ti – Gn 17:7.

Quando Deus fez uma aliança com a nação de Israel no monte Sinai, deu-lhe a Lei, que continha os termos e as condições da aliança mosaica.

Hoje, em nossas Bíblias, temos o Antigo e o Novo Testamento. Isso se refere à Antiga e à Nova Aliança. No Novo Testamento temos os ensinamentos de Jesus e de seus apóstolos, que se sobrepõem à lei do Antigo Testamento. No Sermão do Monte, Jesus disse repetidamente: “Ouvistes que foi dito, mas eu vos digo”.

O autor de Hebreus disse o seguinte a respeito da Nova Aliança: Mas agora alcançou ele ministério tanto mais excelente, quanto é mediador de uma melhor aliança, que está firmada sobre melhores promessas – Hb 8:6.

No dia do casamento, usamos palavras de significado preciso para estabelecer uma aliança vinculante: “... até que a morte nos separe”. Os votos de casamento podem variar um pouco, mas devem sempre incluir o compromisso com um relacionamento de amor mútuo, vinculante por toda a vida e, portanto, irrevogável.

Testemunhas

Outra parte importante de uma aliança são as testemunhas. As testemunhas validam os votos feitos e asseguram a prestação de contas. Isso é especialmente verdadeiro em uma aliança feita entre duas pessoas.

Quando Josué restabeleceu a aliança com Israel ao entrar na terra de Canaã, desafiou o povo: E Josué disse ao povo: Vós sois testemunhas contra vós mesmos de que escolhestes o SENHOR para o servir. E disseram: Somos testemunhas – Js 24:22. O que estavam dizendo era: “Responsabilizaremos uns aos outros pelos compromissos que estamos assumindo hoje”.

Quanto à Nova Aliança, temos o testemunho do apóstolo João, que diz: Porque três são os que dão testemunho no céu: o Pai, a Palavra e o Espírito Santo; e estes três são um. E três são os que dão testemunho na terra: o Espírito, a água e o sangue; e estes três concordam num – 1 Jo 5:7-8. Aqui João está dizendo que, nessa Nova Aliança entre Deus e o homem, há três testemunhas no céu e três testemunhas na terra, e todas essas testemunhas concordam.

Na celebração de uma aliança matrimonial, os convidados do casamento são as testemunhas. Cada convidado se torna testemunha dos votos feitos. Com sua presença e bênção, validam o casamento e se tornam pessoalmente responsáveis por assegurar que esse casamento perdure.

Esse compromisso comunitário com a permanência do casamento é o tecido moral de nossa sociedade e de nossas igrejas. Quando uma sociedade se torna negligente em defender a permanência do casamento, sobrevêm o caos e a confusão. Vemos isso na sociedade que nos cerca. Infelizmente, também estamos vendo um número crescente de casamentos desfeitos em nossas igrejas anabatistas.

Aquilo que ratifica a aliança

A etapa final para estabelecer uma aliança é aquilo que a ratifica e torna vinculantes e eficazes os seus termos. Historicamente, houve diversos métodos de vincular uma aliança. Os antigos beduínos tinham o costume de usar sal para selar uma aliança. Cada parte dava à outra uma porção de sal. O sal era misturado às respectivas reservas de sal, tornando impossível separar “meu sal” do “seu sal”. Isso simbolizava a imutabilidade desse tratado.

Havia também a prática de berith. Berith é uma palavra hebraica que significa “cortar”. No antigo Israel, uma aliança era ratificada por meio de “cortar uma aliança”. Essa prática é claramente ilustrada em Gênesis 15, quando Deus ratificou sua aliança com Abraão. Abraão perguntou a Deus: ... Senhor DEUS, como saberei que hei de herdá-la? – Gn 15:8. Deus respondeu ao pedido de Abraão: ... Toma-me uma novilha de três anos, uma cabra de três anos, um carneiro de três anos, uma rola e um pombinho – Gn 15:9. Abraão tomou esses animais, cortou-os ao meio e dispôs as partes como sacrifício a Deus. Deus reafirmou sua aliança com Abraão (com palavras) e, em seguida, no versículo 17, temos este acontecimento misterioso: E aconteceu que, posto o sol, houve escuridão; e eis um forno fumegante e uma tocha de fogo que passou por entre aquelas metades – Gn 15:17. Isso era “berith”, ou o “corte da aliança”. Essa cerimônia ratificou e tornou vinculantes os termos e as condições da aliança. Depois desse acontecimento, não há registro de que Abraão tenha alguma vez questionado ou duvidado da promessa de Deus, embora tenha tomado para si a iniciativa de fazer essa promessa se cumprir.

Quando Deus fez uma aliança com Israel no monte Sinai, ... Moisés tomou o sangue, e o aspergiu sobre o povo, e disse: Eis aqui o sangue da aliança que o SENHOR fez convosco acerca de todas estas palavras – Êx 24:8. Esse sangue tornou vinculantes e eficazes os termos e as condições estabelecidos na lei — essa era a Antiga Aliança.

Quando Deus fez uma aliança com você e comigo no monte Calvário, o sangue de Jesus tornou-se a evidência ratificadora, ou o sinal vinculante, de sua Nova Aliança conosco. Quando participamos da comunhão, comemoramos a aliança que temos com Deus por meio de Cristo.

O que ratifica a aliança matrimonial? Como já vimos, no casamento temos palavras (os votos) e testemunhas (os convidados). Isso completa o casamento? Não. O casamento não está completo até que haja união na intimidade física. Isso completa, ou, como às vezes dizemos, consuma a aliança matrimonial. É isso que ratifica e torna vinculantes e permanentes os termos e as condições da aliança matrimonial. Já no início das Escrituras temos um exemplo disso: E Adão conheceu Eva, sua mulher... Gn 4:1. Mais adiante, vemos outro exemplo: E Isaque levou Rebeca para a tenda de sua mãe Sara, tomou Rebeca, e ela se tornou sua mulher; e ele a amou... – Gn 24:67. A união física faz parte da aliança. É por isso que tal relacionamento fora do casamento é pecado. A fornicação ou o adultério toma aquilo que Deus ordenou que estivesse inseparavelmente ligado ao casamento e corrompe a aliança.

Quando um casal casado se une fisicamente, comemora e celebra sua aliança matrimonial. Esse é o começo do estabelecimento de uma realidade bíblica de “uma só carne”. Dessa união abençoada surge uma nova vida na forma de preciosos “pequeninos” e de corações renovados pelo poder do amor.

Quando participamos do pão e do vinho da comunhão, comemoramos e celebramos nosso relacionamento de aliança com Cristo. Dessa união abençoada surge uma nova vida na forma de corações renovados pelo poder do amor. Essa é a força da aliança.

Onde existem esses três elementos — votos, testemunhas e aquilo que ratifica — há um relacionamento de aliança. Em que um relacionamento de aliança difere de qualquer outro relacionamento?

Um compromisso de fidelidade

Algumas das palavras mais nobres que os lábios humanos podem pronunciar são: “Prometo amar você até que a morte nos separe”. No dia do casamento, é fácil pronunciar essas palavras, e talvez sejamos muito sinceros ao dizê-las. O fato é que ninguém pode saber o preço que essas palavras poderão custar ao longo de uma vida.

O amor é uma escolha e precisa ser estabelecido e perseverar como uma prática diária de vida. Precisamos escolher dirigir nosso afeto à pessoa a quem nos ligamos por aliança de amor e afastá-lo das tentações de outras pessoas. Muitos e muitos casamentos são destruídos pela infidelidade.

Deus planejou o casamento para criar um vínculo poderoso. O vínculo espiritual, emocional e físico do casamento cria uma união inseparável. Em Gênesis lemos: Portanto, deixará o homem seu pai e sua mãe, e se unirá à sua mulher, e serão os dois uma só carne – Gn 2:24. A palavra unirá nesse versículo significa “ser soldado ou colado de tal maneira que se torne inseparável”.

Romper o vínculo matrimonial pela infidelidade causa ruptura e feridas em ambas as partes. Satanás, o grande enganador, quer que acreditemos que ser infiel ao cônjuge nos trará algum benefício. Isso é uma grande mentira.

Um compromisso de fidelidade

Deus demonstrou fidelidade à aliança em seu relacionamento com sua noiva do Antigo Testamento — a nação de Israel. Ela não foi fiel aos votos da aliança. Afastou-se da adoração a Jeová e se prostrou diante de altares pagãos. Apesar da infidelidade dela, Deus continuou a buscá-la e a chamá-la de volta para si. A infidelidade de Israel não alterou a fidelidade de Deus. Essa é a força do amor de aliança. O amor de aliança não depende das ações da outra parte. O amor de aliança persiste mesmo sem ser correspondido. Esse é um conceito do Reino. Paulo ensinou: Portanto, se o teu inimigo tiver fome, dá-lhe de comer; se tiver sede, dá-lhe de beber; porque, fazendo isso, amontoarás brasas de fogo sobre a sua cabeça – Rm 12:20. Esse princípio não se aplicaria muito apropriadamente a um casamento desfeito?

A força da aliança só pode ser plenamente compreendida por meio do entendimento do amor divino de Deus por nós. Nossa salvação depende do amor perfeito de Deus por nós. Ele continua a nos amar, embora nosso amor por ele às vezes seja imperfeito. Seu amor infalível continua a nos atrair de volta para si. A força da aliança no casamento está em buscar imitar esse amor divino. Esse amor divino não será encontrado em romances nem em outros livros sobre casamento. Esse amor divino só pode ser encontrado em um relacionamento íntimo com “a Fonte” do amor eterno.
